title: General Software Requirements
answer:
Before installing Modern Requirements4DevOps, your machine needs:

1. Operating System: Windows Server 2019 or 2022 (both 32-bit and 64-bit supported)
2. Browser: Microsoft Edge, Internet Explorer 10+, Chrome, or Firefox 47.0.1+
3. Screen resolution: 1280 x 960 or higher
4. IIS: version 7 or higher
5. Microsoft .NET Framework: 4.5 or higher
6. ASP.NET: version matching your installed .NET Framework (e.g. .NET 4.7.2 → ASP.NET 4.7.2)
7. Multilingual support: Language Pack for IE & Save as Word

The account installing the application needs administrator rights on the machine, and for regular team projects, admin rights on the TFS Collection (or added in the application domain in IIS).

Important: for HTTPS, the application must be bound with a trusted CA-signed SSL certificate — a self-signed certificate isn't supported.

title: Supported Microsoft Word Versions
answer: For Word Import, Modern Requirements4DevOps supports Microsoft Word 2010 or higher, with .docx, .dotx, .docm, and .dotm file extensions.

title: Team Foundation Server Requirements
answer: For the embedded build with Single Sign-On, Modern Requirements4DevOps requires Azure DevOps 2019 or 2022.

title: Hardware Requirements
answer: Minimum hardware: at least 32 GB of RAM (or higher) if you're executing TFS work item queries greater than 100,000 items, and 256 GB of hard drive/SSD space.

title: Minimum Hardware Requirements for Redis
answer: Redis uses approximately 477.8495 KB (0.4666 MB) of memory per user. The maximum hard drive space required is 1.5 × your memory size — e.g. 8 GB of RAM means up to 12 GB of hard drive space for Redis. Make sure your machine has sufficient hardware before installing.

title: Installation Guidelines
answer:
Users get a single installation file: Modern Requirements4DevOps 202x.exe. Since it's web-based, it's best installed on a server, though any machine with IIS 7+ works. Installation is required only once — after that, all users with proper access rights can use it without installing anything locally.

Recommendation: install MR on a separate server or VM from Azure DevOps for better scalability, performance, and to avoid resource conflicts with ADO.

title: Installing Modern Requirements4DevOps — Step by Step
answer:
1. Double-click the Modern Requirements4DevOps 202x Update 1.exe file to start.
2. Check the license terms and conditions checkbox, then click Next.
3. Select the build type: Embedded (recommended) or Standalone.
4. Select the installation type: Single sign-on (TFS 2017 Update 3 / 2018 Update 1 and above only) or Standard.
5. Click Next.
6. Configure the MongoDB installation options and click Next/Install.
7. Configure the Redis Installation options and click Install.
8. Click Yes on the warning message box — the relevant files are copied and installed.
9. Click Finish or Run to complete. For the standalone version, that's the last step.

For the embedded version, a TFS deployment instruction page opens after Finish, walking you through deploying the TFS Extension using the generated VSIX file.

title: MongoDB Installation Options
answer: Auto Install/use existing MongoDB is recommended if MongoDB isn't already on the target machine. If it is, provide the machine name/IP where it's installed (same for a load-balancing server). The default MongoDB port is 27017 — use the same port you used during MongoDB's own install if different. Get the MongoDB user/password from your network department if set. The Replica Set field is for data replication/mirroring.

title: Redis Installation Options
answer: Auto Install/use existing Redis is recommended if Redis isn't already installed. If it is, provide the machine name/IP (same for load-balancing setups). The default Redis port is 6379. Get the Redis password from your network department if applicable. The password and Use SSL options aren't mandatory — it depends on your organization's procedures.

title: Installing a Modern Requirements4DevOps Patch
answer:
Patches include important updates and require the core MR4DevOps release to already be installed. Patches are cumulative — if Patch 2 is released after Patch 1, installing Patch 2 alone includes everything from Patch 1.

To install: navigate to the relevant folder, double-click the patch .exe file, and click Close once it completes.

title: Patch Version Info
answer: A change to the fourth digit of the build version means a patch with bug fixes was released on that build (there can be multiple patches per build). Check your current build version and license status under Organization Settings → Modern Requirements4DevOps → Licensing in Azure DevOps.

title: Deploying the TFS Extension Using the VSIX File
answer:
1. Log into your TFS.
2. Click the Marketplace icon, then select Manage extensions.
3. Click Browse local extensions.
4. Click Manage extensions, then Upload new extension.
5. Click Browse, select the VSIX file generated at the end of installation, then click Upload.
6. Select the desired team project collection and click Continue.
7. Review the requested permissions (Code read/write/manage, Code status, Identity read, Work items read/write) and click Confirm.

Afterward, the Modern Requirements4DevOps Embed options appear under the Work tab (Diagram, Simulation and Use Case, Review, Trace Analysis, Baseline, etc.).

title: Can't Find the VSIX File? — GUI Method
answer:
You can generate the VSIX manually two ways: via Windows GUI or Command Prompt.

GUI method:
1. Go to the Modern Requirements4DevOps installation folder (e.g. C:\Program Files (x86)\Modern Requirements\Modern Requirements4DevOps 2019 Update 2).
2. Open TFS Extension Maker, then the Standard or Single Sign On folder matching your install type.
3. Double-click TFSExtensionMaker.exe.
4. Provide the Modern Requirements4DevOps URI (e.g. http://steve:8028) and an Output Directory, then click Generate.
5. Click OK — the VSIX is created at that location (you'll be asked before overwriting an existing one).

Then follow the normal 'Deploying TFS Extension' steps to deploy it.

title: Can't Find the VSIX File? — Command Prompt Method
answer:
1. Open Command Prompt as Administrator.
2. Navigate to the TFS Extension Maker folder inside your installation folder (e.g. ...\Modern Requirements4DevOps 2019 Update 2\TFS Extension Maker\Standard).
3. Run:
TFSExtensionMaker.exe --baseuri "http://<server name>:8028" --out "<Output directory path>" --override true --publisher "edevtech-mr" --version <TFS Extension Maker version> --scope "full" --exttype "project"
4. Check the output location for the .vsix file.
5. In a browser, go to http://<server name>:8028/VSOInteGreat4TFS/EmbedOMInstructions and follow the on-page instructions to deploy it.
6. Once installed, go to the project → Manage Features / Preview Features, and enable the modules you want — they'll then appear under the Work tab.

title: Updating the Extension
answer:
When updating with a newly created VSIX, uninstall and remove the existing MR extension first to avoid version-control errors — don't upload the new VSIX on top of it.

1. Delete from the Extension Page: go to Extensions in Azure DevOps, find Modern Requirements4DevOps, click Uninstall.
2. Remove from Manage Extensions: go to Manage Extensions, select the extension, click Remove, and confirm.

Only then upload the new VSIX file.

title: Activating the Embedded Version
answer:
1. Access your TFS in a browser and select Modern Requirements4DevOps under the Settings (gear) tab.
2. If not activated, you'll see 'Your product is not activated' with an Activate License option.
3. Click Activate — you're taken to the License Activation page, where you choose User Based, Floating, or Offline Activation.

title: User Based Activation
answer:
1. Select the User Based license type (if not already) — your license binds to the provided username.
2. Enter the license key and click Activate.

On success, you're taken to the Browse page to open any team project.

title: Floating Activation
answer:
1. Select the Floating license type.
2. Enter the Floating URL and click Activate.

On success, you're taken to the Browse page to open any team project.

title: Offline Activation
answer:
For a machine without internet access:
1. Select the Activate Offline checkbox.
2. Click Generate Request File.
3. Email the generated request file to support@modernrequirements.com.
4. Once you receive a license file back, click Apply License File to complete activation.

title: Activation Unsuccessful Error
answer:
This is almost always an internet connectivity issue. If a firewall or proxy is blocking the connection, ask your network/IT department to whitelist:
https://modernrequirements.compliance.flexnetoperations.com:443/deviceservices

Once allowed through, retry activation.

title: Configuring redirectUri for MR Credentials (Azure DevOps Services only)
answer:
This only applies on Azure DevOps Services (VSTS) — not Embedded/Standalone installs on your own machine.

1. Open IIS Manager.
2. Select ModernRequirements4DevOps UI under Sites.
3. Open Application Settings.
4. Find redirectUri and double-click to edit.
5. Set the Value to your base URL and port, e.g. https://steve:8028/
6. Click OK to save.

Skip this and MR Credentials will fail during E-Signature approval in Review — you'll see a Microsoft sign-in prompt followed by a 'This site can't be reached / localhost refused to connect' error.

title: Enabling Third-Party Cookies — Google Chrome
answer:
Modern Requirements4DevOps requires third-party cookies to be enabled.

In Chrome:
1. Click the three dots (top right) → Settings.
2. Click Privacy and security → Third-party cookies.
3. Select Allow third-party cookies.
4. To scope it to just your MR site, scroll to 'Sites allowed to use third-party cookies', click Add, enter the site URL (e.g. https://dev.azure.com), and click Add.

title: Enabling Third-Party Cookies — Microsoft Edge
answer:
In Microsoft Edge:
1. Click the three dots (top right) → Settings.
2. Click Privacy, search, and services → Cookies and site permissions.
3. Toggle off Block third-party cookies, or scroll to 'Allowed to save cookies' and click Add site.
4. Enter the site URL, check 'Include third-party cookies on this site', and click Add.

title: Enabling HTTPS
answer:
By default, Modern Requirements4DevOps runs on port 8028 (<Host Name>:8028). To use HTTPS or a different port:
1. Run inetmgr (IIS Manager) via Windows Run.
2. Expand the root node, then Sites.
3. Right-click your Modern Requirements4DevOps site → Edit Bindings.
4. Click Add, change Type from http to https.
5. Enter your desired port (e.g. 443).
6. Select your SSL certificate and click OK.

The certificate must be a trusted CA-signed certificate — self-signed certificates aren't supported.

title: What the Test Case Management guide covers and who it is for
answer:
Modern Requirements NextGen brings the test plan, the tests, the results, and the reasons behind those results into one place on top of Azure DevOps. Azure DevOps' built-in reporting only understands Test Plans, Test Suites and Test Cases — everything that happens once testing starts (runs, pass/fail results, step outcomes, screenshots, tester comments, bugs) is hard to report on natively. Modern Requirements NextGen closes that gap.

Who it's for: testers, test leads, business analysts, and project managers working with Azure DevOps Test Plans alongside Modern Requirements NextGen. No technical background is needed — everything is done through menus, checkboxes and dropdowns.

Test reporting is available in two places: Smart Report (Test Plans hub, Smart Docs, Queries), where reports appear as formatted documents, and Trace Analysis, where they appear as an interactive matrix.

title: The building blocks a test report is made from
answer:
A test report in Modern Requirements NextGen is assembled from these building blocks:

- Test Plan — the overall test plan the report is based on.
- Test Suite — a group of test cases within the plan.
- Requirement Category — the requirement (user story, backlog item, etc.) a suite was created to verify; only appears when a suite is linked to a requirement.
- Test Case — an individual test, including its steps.
- Test Point — one specific instance of a test case: that test case, in one suite, run against one configuration.
- Test Run — one testing session, manual or automated.
- Test Result — the outcome of a test case for one run (passed, failed, blocked, etc.).
- Test Step Run — the outcome of one individual step within a test result.
- Bug — a bug filed because of a failed test.

Test Plan, Test Suite, Test Case and Bug are native Azure DevOps items. Requirement Category, Test Point, Test Run, Test Result and Test Step Run are virtual work items added by Modern Requirements NextGen and linked in automatically. You choose which blocks to include and NextGen assembles them into a single connected report, whether as a Smart Report document or a Trace Analysis matrix.

title: Fields available for Test Suite and Requirement Category
answer:
Test Suite fields: ID (the suite's identifier), Title (the suite's name), State (the suite's current state).

Requirement Category fields: ID (the requirement's identifier), Title (the requirement's name), Work Item Type (User Story, Product Backlog Item, Requirement, or a custom type your organization uses).

These fields are added to a report through Column Options in Trace Analysis, or the Report Designer in Smart Report.

title: Fields available for Test Point and Test Run
answer:
Test Point fields: ID (the test point's identifier), Title (the test case name), Outcome (Passed, Failed, Active, etc.), Last Step Expected Result (the anticipated outcome of the test case's last step), Last Step Run Comment (observations recorded during execution of that last step).

Test Run fields: ID (the run's identifier), Title (the run's name), Attachment (any file attached to the run itself from the Run Summary tab in Azure DevOps).

title: Fields available for Test Result
answer: Test Result fields: ID, Title, Outcome (the outcome of this particular result), Config Name (the test configuration the result was produced against), Detail Comments (the comments recorded for each attempt during execution — click the link to view), Comment (a comment added afterwards, when reviewing or updating the result rather than while executing it), Result Attachment (files attached to the result while it was being executed — click the link to view), Test Parameter (the parameter values used by this result), and Details (the full breakdown of each individual attempt/iteration, including its own comment and attachments).

title: Fields available for Test Step Run
answer: Test Step Run fields: ID (the step's identifier), Title (the step's action), Comment (the note recorded against this step, typically when it is marked failed — click the link to view it), Attachment (any screenshot or file captured against this step — click the link to view it), Test Parameter (the parameter value used by this step, if the test case is parameterized).

title: Where you can build a test report
answer:
Test reporting can be generated from wherever you're working:

- Smart Report from the Test Plans hub — right-click a Test Suite under Test Plans in Azure DevOps and choose Smart Report. Gives a formatted report for that suite, and optionally its sub-suites, with runs and results.
- Smart Report from Smart Docs — insert Test Plan, Test Suite or Test Case items under any hierarchy, then generate the Smart Report. Merges the related test information into your document.
- Smart Report from Queries — open a query that returns test cases, then choose Smart Report from the toolbar. Covers the tests your query returned.
- Trace Analysis (Horizontal Matrix, Mode: Test reporting) — a complete test report as an interactive hierarchy/matrix.

Note: for test reporting, you can also generate smart reports containing the test execution data.

title: Designing a Smart Report template in the Report Designer
answer: Smart Report renders test information as a formatted document. Every building block (Test Plan, Test Suite, Requirement Category, Test Case, Test Point, Test Run, Test Result, Test Step Run, Bug) is available as an item type in the Report Designer, so you can create a section for each one you want to include. Pick a building block from the item type dropdown to start a new section for it, then add the fields you want to show from that item's field list.

title: Generating a Smart Report from the Test Plans hub (Generate Report vs. Suites Hierarchy)
answer:
Right-click a Test Suite under Test Plans in Azure DevOps and choose Smart Report to open the module scoped to that suite. Two generation options are offered:

1. Generate Report — shows data pertaining exclusively to the Test Suite the Smart Report was invoked from, for users who want to focus on that single suite's insights and metrics.
2. Generate Report Including Suites Hierarchy — opens a pop-up letting you select the invoking Test Suite along with its child suites via checkboxes, so you can choose one, several, or all suites to include in the report.

When generating with the suite hierarchy included, up to 25 suites are auto-selected at a time; an administrator can raise this limit if you need more.

title: Filtering a Smart Report by Test Configuration
answer: The Settings icon on the Smart Report's Report tab opens a test configuration picker for the project. By default, all configurations are selected. Narrow the selection to generate the report with test results only for the selected test configurations (e.g. a specific OS or browser).

title: Generating a Smart Report from Smart Docs
keywords: insert test plan test suite test case
answer:
You can generate comprehensive test reports directly from Smart Docs — the report consolidates test information for the work items included in the Smart Doc, letting you review test coverage and results alongside your documented requirements.

Tip: insert a Section or a Requirement item first, then add Test Plan, Test Suite and Test Case items beneath it (created from the Test Plan hub and added via the right panel) to build full traceability from requirement to test result within a single structured document.

title: Generating a Smart Report from the Queries tab
keywords: query must return test plan suite case
answer:
Smart Report can also be generated from a work item query. For the test-specific information to come through, the query needs to return Test Plan, Test Suite and Test Case items — otherwise that part of the report will not be generated. If the query also returns other items such as Bugs, those are included the normal way, on the same smart part containing all the test-related work items.

Note: linking of virtual work items is supported only when the report is generated from the toolbar.

title: Starting a test report in Trace Analysis: Type of Matrix and selecting Test Plan/Suite
answer: In Trace Analysis, test reporting is one of the modes available when creating a new matrix. Set Type of Matrix to Horizontal and Mode to Test Reporting to open the test report editor. Choose a single Test Plan from the plans available in your project, then choose one or more of its Test Suites — you can generate a report for one suite on its own, or several at once.

title: Filtering by Test Configuration and choosing what to include in a Trace Analysis report
answer:
In Trace Analysis you can choose one or more Test Configurations (e.g. a browser or OS) to scope the report to; by default every configuration in the project is included.

Every building block is listed with a toggle next to it — turning a toggle On adds that level to the report, Off leaves it out, so the report stays focused on exactly what you need. The Requirement Category toggle only becomes available once you've selected a suite that is linked to a requirement; when enabled, it's automatically added beneath that suite.

title: Column Options and required building block combinations in Trace Analysis
keywords: test result needs test run or test point
answer:
Each level included in a Trace Analysis report has its own Column Options, where you choose exactly which fields appear for that level (from the properties in the Virtual Work Item Properties section). Only fields relevant to that level are offered.

Required building block rules:
- A Test Suite needs a Test Plan above it.
- A Test Case, Test Point, or Requirement Category needs a Test Suite above it.
- A Test Result needs something to attach to: a Test Run, a Test Point, or a Test Case.
- A Test Step Run and a Bug both need a Test Result above them.

If a required building block is missing from your selection, the row is outlined so you can see what needs fixing before you run the report. See the Report Paths reference for the valid combinations.

title: Where test attachments show up in a report, based on where they were added
answer:
Attachments recorded during testing are picked up automatically wherever the report is generated (Test Plans hub, Smart Docs, Queries tab). Where an attachment appears depends on where it was added while the test was being run:

- Added to a test run from the Run Summary tab → appears under Test Run as an "Attachment" link.
- Added to a result while running a test case with no step selected (also covers Capture user actions, Record screen, and Record screen with audio) → appears under Test Result as a "Result Attachment" link.
- Added to an individual step using Capture screenshot while executing that step → appears under Test Step Run as an "Attachment" link.

Each of these fields can be added to a report the same way as any other field — via the Report Designer in Smart Report, or Column Options in Trace Analysis.

title: Where test comments show up in a report, based on where they were entered
answer:
Comments recorded during testing are also surfaced automatically:

- Entered on a result while executing a test, for each attempt → appears under Test Result as "Detail Comments", with every attempt's comment kept as its own line so nothing is lost.
- Entered on an individual step, typically when it's marked failed → appears under Test Step Run as "Comment".

title: Shared Steps and Test Parameters in a report
answer: Shared steps and parameters used within test case steps are tracked all the way through to the report. Add the "Test Parameter" field to see the parameter values used in a test case, and the "Actions" field to see its steps, including any shared steps. Both are available through the Report Designer in Smart Report and Column Options in Trace Analysis.

title: Reporting by Requirement (Requirement Category)
keywords: user story product backlog item custom type
answer:
A requirement-based test suite is how Azure DevOps ties tests back to what they're meant to verify — creating a suite from a requirement automatically fills it with the linked test cases. Modern Requirements NextGen surfaces that requirement as its own level (Requirement Category) sitting under the Test Suite. This works regardless of what your project calls its requirements (User Story, Product Backlog Item, Requirement, or a custom type), with no extra configuration needed.

In Smart Report, the Requirement Category section of the template is filled in automatically for requirement-based suites. In Trace Analysis, the Requirement Category checkbox becomes available once a requirement-linked suite is selected.

title: Reference: valid report paths you can build (structure-only, run-rooted, plan-rooted, requirement-rooted)
answer:
The building blocks can be combined in several valid ways (see Section 6.5 rules for what each block requires above it). Common groups of paths:

Structure only: Test Plan > Test Suite; Test Plan > Test Suite > Test Case; Test Plan > Test Suite > Test Point.

Rooted in a Test Run: Test Run; Test Run > Test Result; Test Run > Test Result > Test Step Run; Test Run > Test Result > Bug; Test Run > Test Result > Test Step Run > Bug.

Rooted in a Test Plan, with execution and bugs: Test Plan > Test Suite > Test Run > Test Result > Bug (and variants adding Test Step Run, Test Case, or Test Point into the chain).

Without a Test Run: Test Plan > Test Suite > Test Case > Test Point > Test Result (and variants adding Test Step Run and/or Bug); Test Plan > Test Suite > Test Point > Test Result > Bug (and with Test Step Run).

Requirement-rooted: Test Plan > Test Suite > Requirement Category > Test Case (or Test Point) > ... > Test Result > Test Step Run > Bug, in several combinations.

23 named paths in total are documented — use the one that matches whether you're reporting structure only, execution results, or requirement traceability.

title: Good to know: suite limits, valid combinations, and query requirements for test reports
keywords: query must return test plan test suite test case
answer:
A few things to keep in mind when working with test reports:

- When generating a Smart Report from the Test Plans hub with its suite hierarchy included, up to 25 suites are auto-selected at a time. If you need more, your administrator can raise this limit.
- The report needs to start from a valid combination of building blocks — a Test Suite needs a Test Plan above it, a Test Case/Test Point/Requirement Category needs a Test Suite above it, a Test Result needs a Test Run/Test Point/Test Case above it, and a Test Step Run or Bug needs a Test Result above it.
- When generating from a query, make sure it returns Test Plan, Test Suite and Test Case items — otherwise the test-specific part of the report will not be generated.

title: What is the Cross Reference feature
answer: The Cross Reference feature lets users add references on the grid or at the work item level, improving the organization and accessibility of information. Users access it via the Cross Reference option available in the right panel dropdown.

title: Cross Reference tabs: Insert and All References
answer: When the Cross Reference tab is opened in the right panel, it contains two sub-tabs: 'Insert' and 'All References'. The Insert tab is used to insert references, while the All References tab shows a consolidated view of all references associated with the selected work item. This tab-based layout is meant to streamline managing and navigating references.

title: Insert tab: selecting a reference type and the required-selection error
answer: The Insert tab is selected by default when the Cross Reference tab is opened. Before inserting any reference, the user must first select a reference type from the Reference type dropdown. If a reference type is not selected, an error message appears in the top-right corner of the screen. Selecting a reference type is required before the user can place a cursor on the grid and proceed with reference insertion.

title: Reference types: Numbered item, Table, Image
answer: There are three reference types available in the Insert tab: 'Numbered item' - all numbered items on the grid fall under this type, but only an ordered list created in the Smart Editor (in a work item field) counts as a Numbered item for cross reference; an 'Unordered list' from the Smart Editor is NOT supported, and a number that merely appears alongside the work item title cannot be referenced. 'Table' - only a table caption inserted via the Smart Editor can be used for cross reference. 'Image' - only an image caption inserted via the Smart Editor can be used for cross reference.

title: How reference points populate after choosing a reference type
answer: Once a reference type is selected from the Reference type dropdown, the system automatically populates the list of relevant numbers and captions for that reference type, shown below the dropdown, so users can pick the reference points they need. Along with this list, checkboxes such as 'Insert as hyperlink' and 'Append parent numbering' may also appear, giving users additional customization options.

title: All References tab: viewing references and single-item limitation
answer: The All References tab displays the references for the selected work item(s) in sequential, structured order, making it easy to locate and review referenced items. Note: if more than one work item is selected on the grid at the same time, the Insert tab becomes disabled.

title: Deleting a reference from the grid or All References tab
answer: Users can remove a reference from both the grid and the Cross Reference tab by hovering the mouse over the reference to be deleted and clicking the 'X' icon. This deletion option is available within the All References tab of the Cross Reference section, allowing users to keep their referenced items accurate and up to date.

title: Confirming reference deletion (OK button)
answer: After clicking the X icon to remove a reference, the user must click the 'OK' button to confirm the deletion. Once confirmed, the reference point is deleted successfully.

title: Positioning the cursor to insert reference points on the grid
answer: To add references on the grid, users position the cursor at the work item level within any HTML field. The cursor can only be placed there when the Cross Reference tab is open and a reference type has already been selected. After positioning the cursor, users select the specific reference points (numbers/captions) listed below the Reference type dropdown and checkboxes, which associates the desired references with the corresponding grid or work item.

title: Using the Insert button to add references to the grid
answer: To insert selected references onto the grid or work item, users click the 'Insert' button at the bottom of the Cross Reference tab in the right panel. This button is only enabled once at least one reference has been added/selected. Clicking Insert incorporates the selected references into the grid. The same process (select reference type, select points, click Insert) applies to the other reference types, Table and Image, as well.

title: Insert as hyperlink checkbox
answer: The 'Insert as hyperlink' checkbox, found under Cross Reference Checkboxes, lets users navigate directly to their added reference points. It is checked by default, meaning references are inserted as hyperlinks. When enabled, referenced points in the grid or work item become interactive/clickable links, letting users jump straight to the referenced information.

title: Append parent numbering checkbox
answer: The 'Append parent numbering' checkbox helps distinguish between identical referred items that appear under the same or different work items. It is checked by default, so parent numbering is included when referencing items, appending the parent's numbering to the referenced item for clear identification. Note: if the reference type belongs to the root work item, the reference point is appended with 0, provided this checkbox is checked.

title: What Are Document Properties in MR4DevOps?
answer: Document properties in Modern Requirements let users easily export desired metadata into generated Word/PDF documents. They can be applied from two places: (1) System defined — added from the Admin Panel, where an admin defines a property name and its value is passed by the system directly to a template quick part of the same name during export. (2) User defined — added from the Smart Docs toolbar, where a user defines both a property name and value, which is exported to a template quick part with the matching name.

title: Adding System-Defined Document Properties via the Admin Panel
answer: Document properties can be set up from three places: the Admin Panel, the Smart Docs toolbar, and the Process Template. From the Admin Panel, click the '+ Add' button to add document properties from the list of available document properties — these will then reflect in the exported Microsoft Word and PDF documents. Important: the name of the property created in the uploaded Word template must match (be similar to) the name of the document property defined here in the Admin Panel.

title: Selecting Which Admin Panel Document Properties Appear in Exports
answer: After adding document properties in the Admin Panel, check the box(es) for the properties whose values you want invoked in the exported document. To select all properties at once, check the '[Any]' checkbox at the top of the 'Add Document Properties' pop-up. Note that the 'Approver Details' field is a combined field that pulls data from two other fields: 'Approved By' and 'Approver Role'.

title: Saving Document Properties Set in the Admin Panel
answer: To finish configuring document properties in the Admin Panel, click 'OK' in the properties selection pop-up, then click 'Save Changes' to apply the configuration.

title: Opening the Document Properties Pop-up from the Smart Docs Toolbar
answer: To add user-defined document properties, click the 'Document Properties' option in the dropdown of the extension point ('…') menu on the Smart Docs toolbar. This opens the Document Properties pop-up.

title: Adding or Removing a Document Property Row in Smart Docs
answer: In the Document Properties pop-up (opened from the Smart Docs toolbar), click the '+ Add' button to add a new Document Property Name/Value row, then enter the desired 'Name' and 'Value'. To delete a property row, click the 'X' button next to it.

title: Saving Smart Docs Document Properties and Value Retention Behavior
answer: Click 'OK' to save the user-defined document properties entered in Smart Docs. Any field/value added this way is retained — the values will still be there the next time the user opens the same document. If a property is added but no value is defined for it, nothing for that property will be mapped into the exported document.

title: Document Properties Support in the Process Template (Document Work Item Type)
answer: Document properties are also supported through the Process Template: fields added to the 'Document' type work item in the process template are used as document properties. In Smart Docs, these are shown against the root work item of type 'Document'. The system fetches the values of configured fields (except HTML fields) from that root 'Document' work item, provided the fields are defined via quick parts in the uploaded template. If a value is also defined from the Smart Docs toolbar for the same property, the Smart Docs toolbar value takes precedence over the value coming from the process template's Document work item in the exported Word document.

title: Opening Word's Custom Properties Tab to Map Document Properties
answer: To map document properties into an exported Word/PDF document, the user must define matching custom fields via quick parts in the uploaded Word template. In Word, click 'File', then navigate to Info > Properties > Advanced Properties. This opens a Document Properties pop-up — click the 'Custom' tab to define custom fields.

title: Defining Custom Property Name, Value, and Type in Word (Matching Rules)
answer: On the Custom tab of Word's Document Properties pop-up, enter the property name in the 'Name' textbox and its value in the 'Value' textbox — the 'Type' should always be set to 'Text'. After entering the name and value, click 'Add'; repeat for additional properties. Critical rule: the Property Name entered here must exactly match the name defined in Smart Docs or in the Admin Panel — otherwise the values will not be mapped into the exported Word/PDF document.

title: Inserting a DocProperty Quick Part into the Word Template
answer: To insert a Quick Part for a custom property in the Word template: click the 'Insert' tab, then click 'Quick Parts' and choose 'Field' from the dropdown. In the Field pop-up, scroll the 'Field names' list on the left and click 'DocProperty'. The matching custom property names then appear in the 'Property' column in the center of the pop-up — select the property name you created earlier and click 'OK' to insert it.

title: Table Structure Required for the Approver Details Quick Part in Reports
answer: After inserting a Quick Part, it appears in the document at that location, and the process can be repeated to add all required Quick Parts to design the template. Special requirement: when a report is generated from the review version's toolbar 'Save As' option or from the 'Smart Report' window, and it needs to map 'Approved By' and their 'Roles', the template must contain a table with exactly 3 rows, with the 'Approver Details' quick part placed in the 3rd row, 1st column of that table. Without this table structure, Approver Details will not map correctly in the generated report.

title: What is MR4DevOps Services (MR Agent)?
answer: MR4DevOps Services (formerly called MR Agent) is a component of Modern Requirements4DevOps that is automatically installed with the main application. It is a framework that provides extensibility to Azure DevOps using triggers. MR Services are only accessible with Azure DevOps Services when using a live/public IP to communicate with VSTS (Azure DevOps Services) — if a machine has no public access, Azure DevOps Services cannot be used, and network administrators should set the machine's live IP address and relevant port. MR Services (MR Agent) currently has four sub-components: 1) Custom ID, 2) Suspect Links (formerly called Dirty Flag), 3) Email Monitor, and 4) MatCal. Proper user authentication is required before configuring any of these components — the config files won't work unless the relevant organization (Azure DevOps) or collection (TFS) is registered using authentication.

title: How to configure the AppSettings config file for MR Services
answer: For local Azure DevOps servers (TFS On-Prem), MR Services automatically adds the relevant location in the AppSettings.config file. If Azure DevOps Services are involved, the user's machine must have a live IP address that Azure DevOps Services can use to communicate, and this IP must be added to the AppSettings config file. Steps: 1) Go to the MR Services (MR Agent) installation folder and open AppSettings.config in a text editor — the ApplicationURL is automatically set to the local machine. 2) Change the ApplicationURL value (for Azure DevOps Services only) to the live IP address of your machine plus the relevant port (contact your Network Administrator for this information). 3) Save and close the config file.

title: Timing configurations in the AppSettings file (APPLYALLSCHEDULE, EMAILCHECKSCHEDULE)
answer: At the bottom of the AppSettings config file are timing configuration settings. APPLYALLSCHEDULE works only for Custom ID — it is used to apply Custom ID to newly created work items; the default value of 30 represents the number of minutes after which MR Services scans for new work items and applies Custom IDs, and users can change this value. EMAILCHECKSCHEDULE works only for Email Monitor — it is used to check whether a new email has arrived from which work items could be created/updated; the default value of 15 represents the number of minutes after which MR Services scans for email, and this is also configurable.

title: Registering an Azure DevOps organization for MR Services
answer: To register an Azure DevOps organization for MR Services: 1) Log on to the relevant Azure DevOps Organization and click Organization settings at the bottom left. 2) Scroll down the left side panel and click the Modern Requirements4DevOps option at the bottom. 3) Click the Services option in the Admin Panel — this displays the Services tab options, which are configured further under General Settings.

title: Registering a collection for MR Services in the Embedded version
answer: To register a collection for MR Services in the Embedded version: 1) Launch the embedded version of the application and select the Modern Requirements4DevOps option under the Settings tab — this displays the Admin panel. 2) Click the Services tab — this displays the Services tab options, which are configured further under General Settings.

title: Configuring general settings in the Services Settings tab
answer: The Settings sub-tab under Services handles two things: setting the time interval to scan the Azure DevOps organization (or TFS Collection) for new projects, and registering the current organization (requires admin user credentials). Both are recommended to be configured together. Steps: 1) Enter the Auto Scan time interval (must be between 1 and 60 minutes) — this determines how often the registered Azure DevOps Organization/TFS Collection is scanned for new projects. 2) Provide authorized login credentials with admin rights on the Organization/TFS. For Azure DevOps, only a Personal Access Token (PAT) is allowed for authentication: the 'service username' is the admin's Azure DevOps login email, and the 'service password' is always the PAT. For Azure DevOps Server (TFS), the username and password of the Collection/Organization Administrator are required instead. On successful authentication, the current organization is registered and a confirmation message is displayed.

title: What is Custom ID?
answer: Custom ID is a component of MR Services (MR Agent) used to provide customized IDs to work items in addition to their default work item IDs. Custom IDs do not replace the original IDs — they complement them. Customized IDs can be used to track the origin of a work item, e.g., which team created a particular work item.

title: Custom ID UI options and fields
answer: The Custom ID UI has these options: 1) Scan/Apply Custom ID on new projects — a link to execute Scan and Apply at the same time, scanning for any new/registered project and applying Custom ID configuration to configured work item types that don't have it yet. 2) Custom ID Scope — defines the boundary of the Custom ID counter: Collection applies the counter at the Collection level, Project at the Project level, and Team at the Team level. 3) Custom ID Field — the reference name of the work item field to apply the Custom ID to. 4) No. of Characters for Project name(s) — the default number of characters taken from the Project Name to use as the Project Prefix (tag [PN]) if not explicitly defined. 5) Project Abbreviation — defines an explicit prefix for the selected project, used in Custom ID formatting via tag [PN]. 6) Work item type — defines the work item type(s) Custom ID applies to; multiple types can be selected using a comma separator to group them under the same formatting. 7) Format — defines the format of the ID. 8) Start with — defines the starting sequence of the Custom ID counter.

title: What is Suspect Links (Dirty Flag)?
answer: Suspect Links (formerly called Dirty Flag) is a component of MR Services (MR Agent) used to mark particular work items as suspect — due to changed requirements — so that relevant stakeholders can review these work items once instead of continuing to work from outdated requirements. The Suspect Links option is found under the Services tab.

title: Suspect Links UI options and fields
answer: The Suspect Links UI has these options: 1) Scan for the new projects — applies Suspect Links configuration to newly created projects in the collection. 2) Add new source work item — defines the source work item(s) whose modification can mark associated work item(s) as dirty/flagged when given conditions are met. 3) Pre-state conditional fields — defines the pre-state field criteria of the source work item that must be satisfied first, before watching suspected field(s). 4) Add new property and value — sets the pre-state condition of the source work item. 5) Suspected Field(s) — defines which fields to watch after the pre-conditional criteria of the source work item(s) is satisfied. 6) Target Work Item(s) — tells MR Services which work item type(s) will be tagged as dirty/flagged when a trigger occurs.

title: What is Email Monitor?
keywords: automatic work item creation from email
answer: Email Monitor is a component of MR Services (MR Agent) used to automatically create work items from emails. A particular email address is configured, and once the configuration process is complete, all emails sent to that address result in creating/updating work items.

title: Configuring Email Monitor: prerequisites, default project, and admin email
answer: Before configuring Email Monitor, users must first complete the MR Services user authentication steps (registering the Azure DevOps organization or TFS Collection). Email Monitor settings are divided into sections, each configuring a particular setting, but all necessary settings must be configured at once — users cannot configure some settings and leave others pending. Step 1: click the Email Monitor option. Step 2, in the first section, configure: Admin Email (used as a fallback — if the desired functionality can't be achieved using the address defined in the Email tag, or if criteria don't match the desired values, a warning email is sent to this Admin Email) and Team Project (Default) (defines the default team project for the collection).

title: Configuring Email Monitor: registering the monitored email address and work item type
answer: In the second Email Monitor configuration section, users configure the email address to be monitored along with the relevant work item type and category — the work item type that should be created against emails in Azure DevOps, plus its category, so that if that specific work item type is unavailable, another work item type from the same category is created against the email instead. Clicking Register Email Address opens a popup window where the email's network settings (e.g., SSL, POP3, IMAP) can be configured.

title: Configuring Email Monitor: mapping email content to work item fields and events
keywords: email to work item field mapping
answer: The third and last Email Monitor configuration section defines what information from the email is required to be added into work item fields, and on which events. Events: Add on Creation and Add on Update let the user define on which event(s) the selected information should be added. Fields: Sender Name, Sender Email, and Email Body are the pieces of information from the email that can be added into the work item.

title: Saving Email Monitor settings and starting monitoring
answer: Step 5: click Save Changes to complete the Email Monitor configuration process. Once configuration is complete, users can click the Monitor Emails button to initiate the process of monitoring emails according to the settings that were configured.

title: What is MR MatCal?
answer: MR MatCal is a component of MR Agent used to perform/execute mathematical expressions on work item field(s) and reflect the output on defined field(s) of the same work item. MatCal allows users to define nested expressions for calculation, where the output of one expression can be the input for another. To make MatCal work properly, users must manually create: 1) a folder named after the Azure DevOps (TFS) server name on which MatCal is required to apply, and 2) inside that, under the TFS folder, a folder named after the Azure DevOps Collection/Organization (the same one on which Custom ID is required) — this Collection/Organization folder must contain a config.xml file with all the MatCal configuration.

title: Setting up the MatCal folder structure and config.xml file
answer: To set up MatCal folders: a sample config.xml file is placed in the MatCal folder as the configuration template. Steps: 1) Create a folder named after the Azure DevOps (TFS) server name on which the component is required to apply. 2) Inside that new folder, create another folder named after the Azure DevOps Organization (or TFS Collection) on which the component should apply. 3) Copy the config.xml file (the blueprint for the desired configuration) into this newly created collection/organization folder.

title: Configuring the MatCal config.xml file (CollectionUrl, TeamProjects, MathExpression tags)
answer: To configure MatCal, open config.xml in a text editor and define these tags: CollectionUrl — the URL of the Azure DevOps Organization (or TFS Collection) on which MatCal applies (the URL must not end with a trailing '\'). TeamProjects — lists the team projects to apply MatCal to, using nested ProjectName tags. MathExpression — defines the work item type via the WIType attribute and the field (name or reference name) that receives the output via the OutputField attribute. OnCreate — controls whether the MatCal calculation applies at the time a work item is created (set to 'false' to skip it on creation). OnUpdate — controls whether the calculation applies every time the work item is updated (set to 'false' to skip it on update). Expression — contains the mathematical expression to be evaluated. After configuring, save and close the file. Note: copy-pasting configuration text from the Word/PDF document can corrupt characters (e.g., '–') so that they don't match values that look the same in the UI — it's recommended that users retype field values themselves rather than paste them; this applies to all MatCal examples.

title: MatCal example: basic calculation with a nested expression
answer: Example 1 (applying a calculation): For a Risk work item, Original Estimate = (Priority + Severity) * Probability, where Severity must first be converted to a numeric value via a nested MathExpression. Configuration: <MathExpression WIType="Risk" OutputField="Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.OriginalEstimate" OnCreate="true" OnUpdate="true"><Expression>(Priority + severityVal) * Probability</Expression><MathExpression OutputField="severityVal"><Expression>If (Severity = "1 - Critical", 1, If (Severity = "2 - High", 2, If (Severity = "3 - Medium", 3, 4)))</Expression></MathExpression></MathExpression>.

title: MatCal example: applying multiple conditions
answer: Example 2 (applying multiple conditions): For a Risk work item, Severity is derived from Probability thresholds: if Probability > 80, Severity = '1 – Critical'; if between 40 and 80, Severity = '2 – High'; if between 10 and 40, Severity = '3 – Medium'; otherwise Severity = '4 – Low'. Configuration: <MathExpression WIType="Risk" OutputField="Severity" OnCreate="true" OnUpdate="true"><Expression>If (Probability < 10, "4 – Low", If (Probability < 40 AND Probability >= 10, "3 – Medium", If (Probability < 80 AND Probability >= 40, "2 – High", "1 – Critical")))</Expression></MathExpression>.

title: MatCal example: combining calculation and condition
answer: Example 3 (applying calculation and condition): For a Risk work item, if Blocked = No then Probability = Priority * Severity (numeric); if Blocked = Yes then Probability = 50. Severity text values are converted to numbers via a nested expression: '1-Critical'=1, '2-High'=2, '3-Medium'=3, else 4. Configuration: <MathExpression WIType="Risk" OutputField="Probability" OnCreate="true" OnUpdate="true"><Expression>If (Blocked.ToLower() = "no", (Priority * severityVal), 50)</Expression><MathExpression OutputField="severityVal"><Expression>If (Severity = "1 - Critical", 1, If (Severity = "2 - High", 2, If(Severity = "3 - Medium", 3, 4)))</Expression></MathExpression></MathExpression>.

title: MatCal example: string concatenation
answer: Example 4 (applying concatenation): For a Risk work item, Description is set to a concatenation of the Priority and Severity field values with labels. Configuration: <MathExpression WIType="Risk" OutputField="Description" OnCreate="true" OnUpdate="true"><Expression>"Priority: " + Priority + " Severity: " + Severity</Expression></MathExpression>.

title: MatCal example: applying the same rule to multiple work item types
answer: Example 5 (applying the same rule to multiple work items): For Risk and Task work items, if Priority is 1, 2, or 3 then Blocked = Yes; if Priority is 4 then Blocked = No. Multiple work item types are combined in the WIType attribute using a comma separator. Configuration: <MathExpression WIType="Risk,Task" OutputField="Blocked" OnCreate="true" OnUpdate="true"><Expression>If (Priority = 1 OR Priority = 2 OR Priority = 3, "Yes", "No")</Expression></MathExpression>.

title: MatCal example: separate rules for separate work item types
answer: Example 6 (applying separate rules on separate work items): For Feature work items, if Effort > 50 then Priority = 1, else Priority = 4. For Bug work items, if Size > 10 then Blocked = Yes, else Blocked = No. This requires two separate MathExpression blocks, one per work item type: <MathExpression WIType="Feature" OutputField="Priority" OnCreate="true" OnUpdate="true"><Expression>if (Effort > 50, 1, 4)</Expression></MathExpression> and <MathExpression WIType="Bug" OutputField="Blocked" OnCreate="true" OnUpdate="true"><Expression>if (Size > 10, "Yes", "No")</Expression></MathExpression>.

title: Introduction and application setup
answer: This document contains the notes for the 2025 release of Modern Requirements4DevOps (MR4DevOps), describing key features and enhancements of each module, including Version Package, Copilot4DevOps, Smart Docs, Smart Note, FAQ, Diagram, Mock-up, Use Case, Review Management, Trace Analysis, Baseline, Reporting, Smart Reporting, and Impact Analysis. title: 2025 Release Notes Overview
answer: The Modern Requirements4DevOps 2025 Release Notes document (dated 9/3/2025) describes the key features and enhancements for each module in the Modern Requirements4DevOps (MR4DevOps) application, including Version Package, Copilot4DevOps, Smart Docs, Smart Note, FAQ, Diagram, Mock-up, Use Case, Review Management, Trace Analysis, Baseline, Reporting, Smart Reporting, and Impact Analysis. title: General Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Two general bug fixes were included in the 2025 release: (1) an issue where Versions/Review's statuses were collapsing into the first row in Version Management in Smart Docs/Version Package was fixed; (2) an issue where an incorrect version ID was shown in the create request window when initiating a Review/Baseline from the query hub toolbar menu was fixed.

title: Copilot4DevOps Multi-Select Work Items Support
answer: New in the 2025 release: Copilot4DevOps now supports the multi-select feature from Modern Requirements, allowing users to select multiple work items from either the Backlog or Queries tabs and invoke Copilot. Copilot will receive and process the full context of all the selected work items for a more streamlined and efficient workflow. This applies specifically to Copilot4DevOps when accessed through the Modern Requirements application.

title: Copilot4DevOps Homepage Load Fix
answer: Fixed an issue where the Copilot4DevOps homepage did not load on the first attempt and only appeared after reopening. This fix applies to Copilot4DevOps as accessed through Modern Requirements4DevOps.

title: Independent Copilot4DevOps (V6) Updates
answer: For enhancements and fixes available in Copilot4DevOps independently (outside of its integration with Modern Requirements4DevOps), users should refer to the official 'Copilot4DevOps V6 - Release Notes.pdf' document. Only the Copilot4DevOps updates specific to Modern Requirements4DevOps (multi-select support and the homepage load fix) are documented in this MR4DevOps 2025 Release Notes.

title: Approver Role Requirement Setting in Admin Panel
answer: A new section called 'Require Role Assignment for Approvers' has been added to the Admin Panel, letting admins make role assignment mandatory for all approvers in a review. When enabled, the Review Initiator must assign a role to each approver before sending the review request. The checkbox 'Make role assignment mandatory for approvers during review creation' is unchecked by default so current behavior is unchanged. This feature helps ensure all approvers have clear roles before a review is initiated.

title: Version Packages Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Three bug fixes were made to Version Packages: (1) version comparison failing on the Compare tab for teams other than the default team was fixed; (2) an issue causing unexpected behavior when adding work items with special characters in the title was fixed; (3) an issue where links were not displayed according to the package grid in Smart View when locking a work item was fixed.

title: Test API Report Integration in Smart Docs
answer: Smart Docs now supports seamless integration with the Test API, allowing users to link Test Plans, Test Suites, and Test Cases directly to requirement or section type work items. This enables generating comprehensive reports that reflect full test coverage and hierarchy with reduced manual effort, improving traceability, visibility, and testing efficiency.

title: Smart Docs Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Three bug fixes were made to Smart Docs: (1) fixed an issue where document properties were carried over from one file to another when cloning, using save-as-template, or copying a file; (2) fixed an issue where opening a work item in Azure DevOps (ADO) and saving changes made in the Smart Editor incorrectly redirected the user to the browse page; (3) fixed an issue where options that should stay disabled (permission set to Deny) became enabled again after refreshing.

title: Mandatory Role Assignment for Review Approvers
answer: A new section in the Admin Panel allows role assignments to be made mandatory for all approvers in a review request. When this setting is checked, the Review Initiator must assign a role to each approver before sending the request — the 'Add role' section becomes compulsory and the Role field is highlighted with red borders. Without assigning roles to approvers, the user cannot proceed with creating the review. This feature is fully backward compatible.

title: Comments and Links Count in Feedback Section
answer: The Feedback section in the right panel of a review now displays the number of Comments and Links next to each corresponding label. These counts are also shown in the Audit Reports, making it easier for users to quickly see how many comments and links are associated with a review.

title: Multi-Work Item Selection and Bulk Actions in Review Grid
answer: Review stakeholders can now select multiple work items in the Review Grid and provide a review response on all of them at once. Approvers can Approve or Reject and provide a single comment for all selected work items, and Reviewers can submit reviews or comments in one go. Item-specific options such as Open Work Item, Smart Editor, and Smart View are disabled when multiple work items are selected. Text selection and other view options remain available via a right panel dropdown, based on the review type (reviews created from Review, extension points, Smart Docs, and Version Package). This enhancement is backward compatible.

title: System-Generated Comment Distinction in Reviews
answer: All comments automatically added by Modern Requirements in Review or Feedback Request work items now include the prefix '[Modern Requirements4DevOps generated comment]', allowing users to distinguish between system-added and user-entered comments. This provides transparency and comment traceability during the review process.

title: Highlighted Inactive/Deleted Users in Review Stakeholder Selection
answer: To improve clarity during review creation, inactive or deleted users are now visually distinguished when selected as reviewers or approvers. If an inactive or deleted user is chosen from the drop-down list, it is highlighted with a red border, making it easy to identify and avoid assigning reviews to unavailable accounts.

title: Review Management Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Review Management bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (1) custom states added in a work item not showing immediately in the post states dropdown; (2) the Review browse page getting stuck and not loading properly after renaming a project; (3) Users and Groups not appearing in the reviewers/approvers dropdown on the create request window in a specific scenario; (4) the last work item being cut off after scrolling to the bottom when a review is created with Smart Docs; (5) the Feedback Request work item displaying an invalid name in the 'Assigned To' field in a given scenario; (6) reviews created from Smart Docs or Version Package incorrectly showing live state links instead of only the linked work items from the version the review was created on; (7) the loader not displaying in the create request window when adding bulk work items; (8) the message 'Report(s) are being processed and will attach once completed' not showing when a review with a reviewer included more than 4000 work items.

title: Test Result Count Fields in Test Suite Support (Smart Report)
answer: Test Suites now support detailed count fields in the MR Test API, including Total Tests, Passed, Failed, Blocked, Not Applicable, and Active. These fields are now available in Smart Report, providing clearer visibility into test execution status and improving test coverage analysis.

title: Shared Steps Support in Test API (Smart Report)
answer: Smart Report now supports a detailed representation of Shared Steps within test cases. Users can view Shared Steps and their nested step details, including hierarchical Step IDs, parameters (with multiple values shown comma-separated), outcomes, completion dates, and iteration info. Shared Step names are shown in bold, and outputs are supported in Form, Table, and Form as Table section types.

title: Smart Report Usability and Display Improvements
answer: Several usability and display enhancements were added to Smart Report: (1) users can insert a field clause above a selected row in the Smart Report Designer using the '+' icon — for grouped fields and connected fields shown as a table, adding the clause from the top row excludes it from that grouped field/table, while adding it from any other row includes it in the grouped field/table; (2) the Linked Work Item Type pop-up now displays selected work item types in the order they were added, instead of alphabetical order; (3) unique captions now display for each grouped table, ensuring every table shows its own caption rather than repeating the last one.

title: Smart Report Bug Fixes (2025 Release) - Part 1
answer: Smart Report bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (1) reports not generating per the baseline/review creation version for test case work items; (2) all test suites being auto-selected instead of retaining the originally selected suite when the configured limit was exceeded during report regeneration; (3) table captions not retaining their fields' position on the generated report when multiple table grouping is defined; (4) tables created via the 'make table' option on multiple selected fields not showing the table caption option on reopening the report part; (5) the caption option disappearing when a smart part is reopened after saving; (6) the table caption dialog showing outdated text instead of updating to the new caption when performing Make Table/Untable actions; (7) improper UI appearing when the 'table' option is used on fields in the Smart Report designer; (8) the table caption dialog showing the last changes against fields when multiple table grouping is defined.

title: Smart Report Bug Fixes (2025 Release) - Part 2
answer: Additional Smart Report bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (9) the caption being visible only on the last table rather than all tables when using the make table option; (10) files remaining unsaved on reopening if a field's label is removed; (11) the field filter dialog showing the same values for every field row of the same name; (12) the Save button not being enabled after entering a caption.

title: Test Result Count Fields in Test Suite Support (Trace Analysis)
answer: Test Suites now support detailed count fields in the MR Test API, including Total Tests, Passed, Failed, Blocked, Not Applicable, and Active. These fields are now available in HMTest reporting within Trace Analysis, providing clearer visibility into test execution status and improving test coverage analysis.

title: Horizontal Matrix Generation on Smart Docs Files (Trace Analysis)
answer: Users can now generate a traceability matrix using a Smart Docs file via the Horizontal Matrix Query Type option in Trace Analysis. The Smart Docs file appears in the Select Query dropdown alongside existing query options; users can select any Smart Doc from any folder and generate the matrix according to the work item configuration. Overall functionality — top-level items, linked work items, and fields configuration — remains the same as for normal trace files, and users can generate a Smart Report and export the generated trace data to Excel.

title: Shared Steps Visibility in Trace Analysis
answer: Trace Analysis now fully supports Shared Steps within test cases. Users can view Shared Steps and their nested step details, including hierarchical Step IDs, outcomes, completion dates, iterations, and parameters (with multiple values shown comma-separated). This enhancement gives greater visibility into test execution and improves traceability from requirements to individual test steps.

title: Improved Performance Viewing Test Case Results (Trace Analysis)
answer: The control used for retrieving test case result work items in Trace Analysis was changed to Kendo, improving performance and responsiveness when viewing test case results.

title: Trace Analysis Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Trace Analysis bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (1) Column options not retaining their default field when doing 'Refresh' from the editor; (2) the Column options dialog showing default fields instead of the saved fields for the saved file; (3) an old test case result being shown first instead of the latest result when generating a matrix with a test case work item.

title: Baseline Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Baseline bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (1) newly created PATs failing to authenticate when copying work items to a different Azure DevOps organization; (2) comparison status incorrectly showing 'No Change' when context comparison for links was enabled despite valid changes in work item link relationships; (3) incorrect date and time formats being displayed in the baseline target/source sections despite admin settings; (4) an incorrect 'Ver.ID' being displayed in the 'As of Date' window when the latest date was selected, as well as in the grid after clicking 'OK'; (5) the 'Comp.Status' column showing 'Deleted' for all work items and the 'Comp version.ID' column being blank with a 10k work item baseline in the Compare tab.

title: Diagram Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Diagram bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (1) images added through the media library disappearing when saving as an image or checking in changes; (2) alignment options not working for swimlane shapes within the property popup; (3) the Link Panel not consistently updating when adding links to existing Mockups/Diagrams/Usecases via drilldown; (4) some images disappearing from the diagram and media library after an extended time; (5) the link overlay not being enabled when adding a link to a shape via the right panel until a drill-down action is performed on another shape.

title: Use Case Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Use Case bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (1) steps not showing after a branch step until backspace is pressed; (2) text turning into a hyperlink when selected and made into a Merge and Call Use Case; (3) numbering inconsistency in Alternate Scenarios after deleting a step before it.

title: Smart Note Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Smart Note bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (1) an error message appearing in the top right of the editor when double-clicking an attachment file, with the attachment failing to download; (2) PDF and PPT files becoming corrupted after being inserted into a Smart Note.

title: Document Management Bug Fixes (2025 Release)
answer: Document Management bug fixes in the 2025 release include: (1) File Check-in, Checkout, and Edit being allowed even when 'Deny' is set for a contributor; (2) a file being open-able even when 'Deny' is set against 'Read' in group permission; (3) files not being compared correctly to previous versions.

title: Rights Management overview (project level)
answer: Rights Management in Modern Requirements4DevOps is managed using Permissions and is used to give specific rights to stakeholders of a project. Rights management is done on a per-project basis and is not applicable at the Azure DevOps Organization (TFS Collection) level. The Permission tab is visible to the Collection Administrator (even for projects they are not a member of), while a Project Administrator can only view the Permission tab for their own projects. This feature is currently implemented for 5 modules: Smart Docs, Baseline, Review, Reporting, and Trace Analysis.

title: How to add a new user to an Azure DevOps group
answer: Before rights can be assigned to a user, the user must be added to an Azure DevOps group in the project. Steps: 1) Navigate to the project's home page and click Project Settings. 2) Click the Permission option in the left panel. 3) Under the Groups tab, click the desired group. 4) Click the Members tab. 5) Click Add. 6) Start typing the desired user's name and select from the list. 7) Click Save. The user is now added to the group. To remove a user, select them from the group's member list and click Remove. Note: a collection admin who is not added to any Azure DevOps group in a project cannot access Modern Requirements modules — they must be added as a member of one of that project's Azure DevOps groups.

title: How to access the Permissions (Rights Management) section in Azure DevOps
answer: To access the Permissions (Rights Management) section: 1) Navigate to the home page of the relevant project and click Project Settings. 2) Scroll down and click the 'Modern Requirements4DevOps' option at the bottom of the side panel. The Permissions page is then displayed with all relevant options.

title: Permission rules: Allow, Deny, and Not Set
answer: Permissions are always granted to groups, never to an individual group member (though a group may contain only one member). Group members can be given one of three rights: 1) Allow — explicitly grants access to a group feature; 2) Deny — explicitly restricts access; 3) Not Set — implicitly denies access. Permissions set for a group/team apply to all users in that group/team. By default, 'Project Valid Users' and 'Project Administrators' group permissions are set to Allow for all group features in every Modern Requirements module. 'Project Administrator' can access all modules because of its non-editable default 'Allow' rights — however, if a Project Administrator is also a member of another Azure DevOps group where 'Deny' is set for a feature, that Deny takes precedence over the Project Administrators group setting. The default permission settings of the 'Project Administrators' group are non-editable and independent of inheritance from its parent group.

title: Permission UI overview (two panels)
answer: The Permissions page is divided into two panels: the left-most panel deals with general Azure DevOps options and is not directly involved in Permissions functionality, and the Permissions Settings panel (right side) is used to configure Modern Requirements module/feature permissions.

title: Azure DevOps Groups/Teams panel
answer: This panel consists of all the Teams and Groups fetched directly from the active Azure DevOps project. Addition of new groups/teams, or changes to existing ones, is reflected only after refreshing the browser.

title: Permissions Settings panel structure
answer: The Permissions Settings panel provides permission settings for Modern Requirements modules and features. It is subdivided into a Common Settings section and an individual section for each Modern Requirements4DevOps module: Smart Docs, Baseline, Reporting, Trace Analysis, and Review. Under each section there are Group Features for which permissions can be set to Allow, Deny, or Not Set.

title: Group Features in Permissions
answer: Group Features are sets of individual features grouped together and represented as a single collective 'group feature' (e.g., 'Create/Edit folder', 'Delete folder'). Common group features appear under both the Common Settings section and each module section, while module-specific features appear only under their relevant module section. The specific group features available vary by module.

title: Common Settings section behavior
answer: The Common Settings section contains group features that are common to almost every module section. Values set here are automatically applied to the corresponding feature in each module section. By default, a hyphen (-) is shown for all group features in Common Settings. If a user explicitly sets a value here for a common feature, that value propagates to all module sections. Conversely, if a user changes a common feature's value under an individual module section and different values now exist for that feature across modules, a hyphen (-) automatically reappears in Common Settings for that feature (this also happens if 'Allow & Allow (inherited)' or 'Deny & Deny (inherited)' combinations exist across modules). The Common Settings section works independently for each Azure DevOps group/team and does not inherit from any parent group.

title: Modern Requirements4DevOps Modules section and module access toggle
answer: There is a separate section in the Permissions Settings panel for each Modern Requirements module. A toggle button under each module section allows or prevents users from accessing that module in the application. By default, this toggle is set to 'On' in the parent Azure DevOps group (Project Valid Users), and the same setting is inherited by child groups.

title: How permission inheritance works between parent and child groups
answer: Inheritance occurs between Azure DevOps parent and child groups for permissions on module group features. Permissions set in a parent group are inherited by all child groups (except 'Project Administrators'); changes in the parent propagate to children. By default, permissions are inherited from the 'Project Valid Users' group as follows: if 'Allow' is set on a feature in the parent, 'Allow (inherited)' is set automatically in the child; if 'Deny' is set in the parent, 'Deny (inherited)' is set in the child. By default 'Allow' is set for all features in each module section in Project Valid Users, inherited as 'Allow (inherited)' in child groups/teams. 'Allow' and 'Allow (inherited)' can be overridden to 'Deny' by an admin in the child group, but 'Deny (inherited)' cannot be overridden to 'Allow'.

title: Inheritance scenarios when a user belongs to multiple groups or teams
answer: When a user exists in more than one Azure DevOps group: a) Allow + Not Set => Allow wins (access granted). b) Allow + Deny => Deny wins (access denied). c) Deny + Not Set => Deny wins (access denied). d) Not Set + Not Set => access is implicitly denied. When a user exists in more than one team, the same precedence rules apply (Deny beats Allow beats Not Set beats Not Set), and the resolved value is applied across every team the user belongs to, including the default team.

title: Admin Panel overview and its seven sections
answer: The Admin Panel is used for licensing and for configuring/tweaking options across Modern Requirements modules. To access it, launch the embedded version of the application and select 'Modern Requirements4DevOps' under the Settings tab. The Admin panel has seven sections: 1) Licensing — check license status or activate the product with a valid key. 2) General — configure repository name for GIT projects and other app-wide settings. 3) Smart Docs, 4) Review, and 5) Baseline — tweak options in their respective modules. 6) Version Package — set preferences for storing work item details in version package metadata. 7) Services — configure options related to Services (formerly MR Agent). There is also a Synchronization tab with options to sync application data with the database, used during data migration; it only appears in the Admin Panel upon user request, so most users will not see it.

title: Copilot4DevOps Organization Settings
answer: In the General tab of the Admin Panel, under 'Copilot4DevOps Organization Settings', a checkbox (checked by default) lets an admin show or hide the Copilot4DevOps feature within the Version Package, Smart Docs, and FAQ modules, as well as in the extension point (Queries and Backlog tabs under the work item context menu), at the organizational level.

title: Permission Settings toggle (collection/admin level)
answer: In the General section of the Admin Panel, admins can enable or disable whether the permission settings configured at the project level are applied to features and modules. This checkbox is enabled by default, meaning users' application access follows the permission settings provided at the project level.

title: User Credential configuration (General section)
answer: In the embedded version of the General section, admin/collection user credentials must be provided here to sync MR data to the Azure DevOps Server source control. For Azure DevOps Services, users should instead provide the secondary/alternate user credentials configured in Azure DevOps settings.

title: How to configure a custom project repository name (GIT projects)
answer: This option is not available for the Embedded Single Sign-On version of Modern Requirements4DevOps. By default, the repository is named after the project's name. For GIT projects only, admins can configure a custom repository name: 1) Access the Admin panel and select General. 2) Click +Add. 3) Select the desired GIT project from the list. 4) Enter a suitable repository name and click OK — the new name appears in the list. 5) Click Save Changes.

title: Configure E-mail Settings (SMTP)
answer: In the embedded version's General section, admin/collection user credentials are provided to configure SMTP (email server) settings. Email is sent from various places in the application: Review (review creation, Approver, Reviewer, Resend Reminder, Review Post State Rule, Review cancel, Request Feedback), Smart Report, Baseline, and Trace Analysis (when generating a report exceeding a set threshold) and Impact Analyzer, among other places.

title: Auto Save Layout Settings (Diagram, Simulation, Use Case)
answer: The Auto Save option in the Admin Panel applies to three modules: Diagram, Simulation, and Use Case. For Diagram: auto-save triggers when the user clicks Publish (User Stories, Use Case, or Test Case tab), creates a new or existing link to a page/shape, deletes any link, or performs a drill-down on any shape. For Simulation: auto-save triggers when creating a new/existing link to a page/shape or deleting a link. For Use Case: auto-save triggers when creating a new/existing link to a page/shape or deleting a link.

title: Consider Work Item Links for Comparison (Link Type dropdown)
answer: During comparisons, field values are compared at a basic level; admins can configure whether link type updates should be considered a CHANGE, using the Link Type dropdown under the General section of the Admin Panel. Selected link types are shown yellow-highlighted when comparing revisions in Smart View. Choose 'All Link Types' if any link type change should count as an update; multiple link types can also be selected individually. After selecting the desired link types, click Save Changes.

title: Baseline Compare: Global vs Context link comparison and its toggle button
