answer: In the Baseline Compare tab, work item link comparison can be viewed as Global Comparison (a work item is considered changed if any of its links change, regardless of whether the linked item is inside or outside the baseline compare context) or Context Comparison (a work item is considered changed only if the link change involves a work item that exists within the baseline compare context — i.e., the work items shown under the baseline compare tab during comparison). Link comparison is supported across all three comparison types: comparing a baseline with the current version, comparing with another baseline, and comparing with a query. A toggle button labeled 'Context Comparison for Links' can be shown in the Baseline compare tab if configured from the Admin Panel. To configure it: 1) Go to the General tab in organization settings — by default Global link comparison is selected; deselect it to enable Context Comparison. 2) Select 'Show Context Comparison toggle button in baseline compare tab' and click Save Changes. The toggle is hidden by default; once configured, it appears in the baseline compare tab. When set to ON it enables Context Comparison; when OFF, the default Global Comparison applies. A user's session-level toggle selection persists for that session only — once the session expires, the behavior reverts to the admin panel's configured default.

title: Work Item Configuration: Smart View vs TFS popup, and ADO vs Smart Editor
answer: Clicking a Work Item's title opens either a TFS pop-up (showing the latest revision details) or a Smart View (showing details of the selected revision ID). Admins can configure which popup appears by checking/unchecking a setting in the Admin Panel: if checked, Smart View shows; if unchecked, the TFS Work Item details pop-up shows. Separately, users can configure whether double-clicking a work item in the Smart Docs module (and the Smart Docs View tab in the Review module) opens the ADO Standard Editor or the Smart Editor — check the corresponding Admin Panel setting to open the ADO Editor, or uncheck it to open the Smart Editor.

title: How to configure which work item fields are highlighted in comparisons
keywords: configure work item fields for comparison
answer: Wherever work items are compared, certain fields of the selected work item are shown yellow-highlighted; these fields are configurable via the Admin Panel (fields visible on the Azure DevOps standard editor will show on Smart View). Steps: 1) Access the Admin Panel and click General. 2) Click +Add under 'Configure work item fields for comparison'. 3) Move desired fields from the Available list to the Selected list using the arrow button. 4) Click OK. 5) Click Save Changes at the bottom.

title: Configuring the Link Type used for Copy and Clone operations
keywords: link type for copy and clone
answer: When a baseline is copied, users can link original work items to the newly created work items at the target location; similarly when a smart document is cloned, users can link work items in the clone to those in the source. The relationship (link) type used is configurable: 1) Access the Admin panel, select the General tab. 2) Scroll to 'Link type for Copy and Clone' — 'Related' is the default selected link type, but any other link type can be chosen. 3) Click Save Changes.

title: Disregard read-only fields for copy/reuse/clone/rollback/merge features
answer: When using Copy/Reuse in Baseline, Queries, and Backlog tabs, or Clone in Smart Docs, users can specify read-only work item field(s) that should be disregarded (ignored) during the operation, by clicking Add and selecting the desired read-only fields. The same configuration applies to Rollback (from Baseline, Smart Docs, Smart View — Baseline, Review, Queries, and Backlogs) and Merge from Baseline. Any read-only field added to this list is excluded from consideration during these operations.

title: Parameter Configuration in Smart Docs (show/hide Configure Parameter option)
answer: In the Smart Docs module, admins can show or hide the 'Configure Parameter' option via the Admin Panel's General section. Steps: select General Tab, scroll to Parameter Configuration section. Enabling this checkbox shows the 'Configure Parameter' option in Smart Docs; by default the checkbox is disabled/unchecked, so the option is hidden. There is also a dropdown to select the field used as the matching field in the work item where the parameter is referenced (to replace its value) — 'Area Path' is selected by default, but any other field can be chosen.

title: Document Define Properties for Smart Documents
answer: Admins can add document properties for a smart document by clicking Add, so that these properties appear in generated 'Word/PDF as word template' reports (via Smart Report and Save as Word/PDF from the toolbar). Clicking Add lets the user select which document properties to include in the generated reports for a smart document.

title: Document Generation - Apply Table Properties (4 table export checkboxes)
keywords: allow row to break across pages
answer: In the General tab of the Admin Panel, under 'Document Generation - Apply Table Properties', there are four checkboxes applied to every table in exported Microsoft Word/PDF documents (Smart Report, Smart Docs, and Review Audit Reports): 1) 'Allow row to break across pages' — allows all data of a row to display on the same page. 2) 'Repeat as header row at the top of each page' — repeats the table header on each page. 3) 'Fix table content' — resizes the table to fit content so no single word breaks across two lines. 4) 'Fix table window' — resizes the table to the width of the window so it isn't squeezed or exceeds the page width. By default all four checkboxes are unchecked except 'Fix table content', which is checked by default. After configuring, click Save Changes. These settings apply to all section types containing tables. Reports are generated via the Report tab of the relevant module and exported using Save As in MS Word.

title: Date, Time Pattern and Time Zone Settings
answer: In the General tab of the Admin Panel, under 'Date, Time, Pattern and Time Zone Settings', admins can configure how date and time display throughout the application UI and generated documentation. Options include: a checkbox to show date & time in UTC time zone everywhere (checked by default; when unchecked, date/time shows per end-user locale instead); a checkbox to show a timestamp alongside date & time (checked by default); and a selector for the desired Date and Time pattern. The default date format is dd-MMM-yyyy and the default time format is hh:mm:ss tt. Click Save Changes to apply — the selected pattern and time zone then appear throughout the MR application UI and in generated documents.

title: Default font family and font size settings in Smart Editor
answer: In the Smart Docs tab of the Admin Panel, admins can select the default Font-Family and Font-Size shown in the Smart Editor. The default font family is 'Calibri Light' and the default font size is 14, though either can be changed to any other desired value. The selected Font Family and Font Size settings apply to the entire text in the Smart Editor.

title: Configure the 'Area' field as mandatory in Smart Docs 'New File' window
answer: Admins can set the 'Area' field as mandatory (or not) when creating a new Smart Docs file. Steps: go to the Smart Docs tab in the Admin Panel, scroll to "Configure 'Area' field in Smart Docs 'New File' window", and check or uncheck the setting. By default the checkbox is unchecked (Area is not mandatory). Checking the box makes the Area field mandatory when creating a new Smart Docs file via the New File window.

title: Approval Authentication: MR Credentials vs PAT
answer: In the Review tab of the Admin Panel, under 'Approval Authentication', admins can allow users to choose between two authentication methods — MR Credentials and PAT (Personal Access Token) — when granting review approval. This option is checked (enabled) by default. To restrict users to MR Credentials only, deselect the checkbox. For unregistered users, if this option is unchecked, the user must first register through MR credentials before they can grant approval.

title: MR Credentials Settings — password/login credential expiry reminder
answer: Under the Review section of the Admin Panel, 'MR Credentials Settings' lets admins set a reminder for users to update their MR credentials after a given time, as a security measure. This option is only available for users of Modern Requirements4DevOps on Azure DevOps — it does not apply to the Embedded version installed on a user's machine. Admins can configure the login credentials to expire after 30, 60, or 90 days, or choose 'never' (highly not recommended). After the configured period, the password (used to access the application) expires; unless the user updates it before expiry, they will see a password-expired message when attempting to perform an approval via e-Signature. After a password change, the countdown restarts based on the configured expiration value.

title: MR Credentials — Registered Account(s) for Approval management
answer: Under the Review tab of the Admin Panel, the 'MR Credentials-Registered Account(s) for Approval' section lists all accounts registered with MR credentials for approval purposes. Admins can delete accounts that are no longer active/relevant. Steps to delete: select the desired email address and click the adjacent Remove option — the email ID is removed from the registered accounts list. After deletion, that email is no longer visible/accessible in the list, and the user must register again to provide approval on a review.

title: Email Address Configuration for E-Signature failed-attempt notifications
answer: When approving a Work Item in a Review Request, Approvers must provide an e-Signature (login credentials). If three consecutive failed attempts occur, this may indicate an unauthorized approval attempt and the user's account is temporarily blocked; a notification email is then sent to a configured email address. This option is only available for users on Azure DevOps (not applicable to the Embedded version). To add a notification email: 1) Click +Add. 2) Enter the email address and click OK. 3) Click Save Changes at the bottom of the page.

title: Blocked User Settings — temporary account lockout duration
answer: During a Review response, if multiple consecutive failed login-credential attempts occur, the user's account is temporarily blocked. The duration of this blockage is configured via the relevant option in the Review section of the Admin Panel. If an admin decides no blocking is needed, they can choose the '0 minutes' option. This option is only available for Azure DevOps users and does not apply to the Embedded version installed on a user's machine.

title: Data Migration — migrating legacy reviews to the new approach
answer: Admins can bulk-migrate all legacy reviews of a project (created using the previous approach) to the new approach. Steps: 1) Access the Admin Panel and click Review. 2) Scroll to the Data Migration section. 3) Select the desired project from the list. 4) Click Migrate Data. The legacy reviews for the selected project are then migrated. If migration is unsuccessful for some reason, repeat the steps for the failed project(s) only.

title: Auto-generation of Review Audit Reports (bulk, legacy reviews)
answer: This section (regarding legacy reviews, in the upper portion of the Review admin page) lets admins bulk-generate audit reports. Steps: 1) Select the relevant project. 2) Select the relevant From/To dates — if no dates are given, audit reports for all reviews in the selected project(s) are generated. 3) Click Generate Audit Report. The generated audit reports are saved at: %public%\Documents\Review Management\Review Audit Reports\<project name>\. If generation fails for some reason, repeat the steps for the failed project(s) only.

title: Audit Reports Format (Word vs PDF)
answer: By default, Review audit reports are generated in MS Word format; admins can instead select the corresponding option to generate them in PDF format. The selected report format applies to both bulk generation (Admin Panel) and to single reports generated from the audit report option on the Review Toolbar.

title: Configuring Review Response Actions
answer: Admins can configure which actions are available for a review response, adding custom values as needed. Steps: 1) Access the Admin panel and click Review — the Review Response Actions section determines available response actions. 2) Select +Add in the Review Response Actions section. 3) Enter a suitable action name and click OK. 4) Scroll down and click Save Changes.

title: Due Date Configurations for Reviews
answer: The Due Date Configurations section under Review settings lets admins configure several aspects of review due dates: setting a Default Due Date (which appears in the Due Date drop box when creating a new Review Request); allowing initiators to edit the default Due Date; showing or hiding the Due Date field in the Review Request pop-up; allowing initiators to extend the Due Date; and allowing initiators to clear the Due Date. Click Save Changes after configuring.

title: Rules Configurations for the Review Request pop-up
answer: While creating a Review Request, a Rules section appears at the bottom of the dialog box. Admins can configure whether this Rules section is shown at all, and if shown, which specific options within it are displayed. Steps: 1) Access the Admin panel and click Review. 2) Configure which options appear in the Rules section of the Review Request dialog box (disable the top control to hide the Rules section entirely). 3) Scroll down and click Save Changes.

title: Review Non-participant Rights — 'Other Review(s)' access
answer: Traditionally, Modern Requirements4DevOps Reviews were only accessible to their participants: Approvers, Reviewers, and Initiators. This feature, configurable in the Admin Panel, allows access to certain reviews for non-participants as well. When enabled, a new category called 'Other Review(s)' is created in Folder Explorer, allowing non-participants to access such reviews in read-only mode.

title: Send E-mails — configuring which review events trigger automatic emails
answer: Modern Requirements4DevOps can automatically send emails to stakeholders when certain events occur while responding to a review request. Admins configure which events trigger automatic emails by enabling/disabling the relevant checkboxes in this section of the Admin Panel, then clicking Save Changes.

title: Send Reminder — configuring reminder email timing for reviewers/approvers
answer: Modern Requirements4DevOps can automatically send reminder emails to reviewers/approvers so they respond to a review request within the due time. Steps: 1) Access the Admin panel and click Review. 2) Scroll to the Send Reminder section. 3) Select the desired reminder timing (number of days before the deadline) from the list. 4) Click Save Changes.

title: Review Post State Rule — notifying additional stakeholders
answer: When a review request is created, the Post State field (in the Rules section) tells Modern Requirements4DevOps to change the work item's state field to the selected value once the approval process completes. If the selected post state cannot be automatically achieved, the review initiator is notified automatically via email. The Review Post State Rule section (which determines which actions are available for review response) lets admins configure additional stakeholder email addresses to also receive that automatic notification. Steps: 1) Access the Admin panel and click Review. 2) Scroll to Review Post State Rule. 3) Click +Add. 4) Provide the desired email address and click OK. 5) Click Save Changes.

title: Submit Comment — show/hide toggle in Review response
answer: In the Review tab of the Admin Panel, the Submit Comment section lets admins toggle the visibility of the 'submit comment' option in the Review module's Response tab. By default the checkbox is selected (submit comment option is visible); unchecking it hides the submit comment option from the review interface.

title: Configuring work item fields to be copied while copying a baseline
answer: In the Baseline section of the Admin Panel, admins can configure which work item fields (and their default values) are copied when a baseline is copied. Steps: 1) Navigate to the Admin panel, Baseline option. 2) Click +Add in the 'Fields Configuration for Copy baseline' section. 3) Choose the appropriate Work Item type. 4) Select the desired Work Item field. 5) Select the default value for that field. 6) The work item field is added to the list. 7) Click Save Changes.

title: Version Package Metadata — storing work item data (ID only vs configured fields)
answer: In the Version Package tab of the Admin Panel, admins choose how work item field data is stored in metadata for each work item within a package: either 'Work item Id only' or 'Field(s) that are configured in the version package meta template'. After selecting the preferred option, click Save Changes to apply it.

title: Services Section overview (formerly MR Agent)
answer: The Services section of the Admin Panel is used to configure Modern Requirements4DevOps Services options that were previously configured using command prompt instructions (this component was formerly called MR Agent). The guide references a separate detailed resource/link for full information on the Services section rather than covering the configuration steps in-depth on this page.

title: Manually Enabling Windows Features Required for Modern Requirements4DevOps
keywords: turn windows features on or off
answer: If your organization's IT policy restricts users from enabling or modifying the "Windows Features" settings needed for Modern Requirements4DevOps, you can enable them manually: (1) Open Control Panel and set "View by" to Category. (2) Select the Programs option. (3) Under Programs and Features, select "Turn Windows features on or off" - this opens the Windows Features screen. (4) Select the features required for Modern Requirements4DevOps (as highlighted in the installation guide's screenshots). (5) If Windows 8 or a more recent OS version is installed, also enable the additional features highlighted for those newer OS versions.

title: Adding IIS Binding Information in Configuration Files
answer: If you have bound a specific IP address on the system, you must update the web configuration file so Modern Requirements4DevOps points to it: (1) Open IIS Manager by running "inetmgr". (2) Expand the node on the left panel and select Application Pools. (3) Right-click "ModernRequirements4DevOps 2019" and choose Edit Binding to open Site Bindings and see which IP (if any) is bound. (4) Note the bound IP address (e.g., 10.0.0.20), then go to the installation directory: <Drive>:\Program Files\Modern Requirements\ModernRequirements4DevOps 2019\User Interface. (5) Open the Web.config file there in Notepad. (6) Find the tag <add key="ServiceAddress" value="..."/> and change its value from http://<machine name>:8027/ to the bound IP, e.g. value=http://10.0.0.20:8027/. (7) Save and close the file (if you lack permission to save directly in that folder, save to the desktop first, then copy it back and replace the original). (8) Return to IIS Manager and restart both inteGREAT services under the Sites folder.

title: Email Configuration for the Feedback Option (Standalone)
answer: In the Embedded version, email settings are configured via the Admin Panel. For the Standalone version, email configuration must be done manually in the Service's Web.config so the Feedback option in the Simulation Module works (Modern Requirements4DevOps automatically emails stakeholders for feedback, and if email settings are misconfigured these emails fail to send). Steps: (1) Navigate to "C:\Program Files\Modern Requirements\ModernRequirements4DevOps 2019\Service". (2) Copy the Web.config file to another location (e.g., desktop) for editing. (3) Open the copied file in a text editor such as Notepad and locate the mail configuration section. (4) Open your email client (e.g., Microsoft Outlook): go to File > Account Settings > Account Settings, then double-click the relevant email account and note the displayed account information. (5) Click "More Settings", open the Advanced tab, and note the SMTP port. (6) Close Outlook's windows and switch back to the Web.config file. (7) Update the mail settings section in Web.config using the information gathered from Outlook (account details and SMTP port). (8) Save the Web.config file and replace the original file at its installation location (e.g., "...\ModernRequirements4DevOps2018 Update X\Service"). This completes email configuration for the Feedback option.

title: Fix for License Activation Lost After VM Machine Restart (Standalone)
keywords: An error occurred while processing your request
answer: On a Virtual Machine, license activation can be lost after a restart, causing the user to be redirected back to the Activation page or shown the error "An error occurred while processing your request." For a general VM (any OS): (1) Connect to the VM via Remote Desktop. (2) Open Run (Windows key + R) and type "gpedit.msc". (3) Navigate to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > User Profiles. (4) Select "Do not forcefully unload the user registry at user logoff". (5) Change the setting from "Not Configured" to "Enabled" and click Apply, then restart the VM and check if the issue is resolved. If VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is being used instead, follow these steps: (1) Connect to the VM via Remote Desktop. (2) Open Run and type %public%. (3) Open the "Public Documents" folder. (4) Check whether "username.bin" (offline activation) or "username.orf" (online activation) exists. (5) If the file exists, email support@edevtech.com along with the log files located at <Default Drive>:\inetpub\wwwroot\walog. (6) If the file does not exist, ask the VDI administrator to capture and share a VM image taken after activating the license from all users, since that image will retain licensing information for all users.

title: How to Update the Windows Credentials for Modern Requirements4DevOps
answer: During installation, Windows login credentials are provided and saved in Modern Requirements4DevOps settings; if you later change your Windows password, these saved settings become obsolete and can cause problems running the application. To fix this: (1) Open IIS Manager via "inetmgr". (2) Expand the node on the left panel and select Application Pools. (3) Select "inteGREAT4TFSsrv" and click "Advanced Settings" under Edit Application Pool. (4) In the Process Model section, select the Identity option and click its button. (5) Choose "Custom account" and click "Set". (6) Enter the latest Windows credentials in the format <Domain\Username> and click OK to save. (7) Start "inteGREAT4TFSsrv" by clicking Start under Application Pool Tasks. (8) Close all windows to complete the process.

title: How to Use Team Context in TFS 2019
keywords: team drop down internet explorer edge
answer: By default users access an entire Azure DevOps Project, but teams can be restricted to relevant portions of the project by enabling team context: (1) Open IIS Manager via "inetmgr". (2) Expand the node on the left panel, expand the Sites node, and select the "Modern Requirements4DevOps 2019 Update 1" node. (3) Select Application Settings in the middle panel and double-click the "Embed.Tfs2019" entry. (4) Set its value to "true" and click OK. (5) Close IIS Manager. Once enabled, users can select the relevant team of their desired project, and a Team dropdown becomes visible in the User Interface. Note: enabling the Team dropdown means the application will not work in Internet Explorer or Edge browsers.

title: How to Configure Load Balancing for Modern Requirements4DevOps (Overview)
answer: Load balancing for Modern Requirements4DevOps is configured (as a framework, not full installation instructions) in seven steps: (1) Set up/install the desired load balancing environment. (2) Install Modern Requirements4DevOps on all servers. (3) Configure a shared network drive for the shared workspace. (4) Install/configure a shared Redis server. (5) Change the User Interface Configuration file (web.config). (6) Change the Service Configuration file (web.config). (7) Repeat steps 5 and 6 on every server where Modern Requirements4DevOps is installed for load balancing. Note that steps 5 and 6 refer to two different files that happen to share the same name (Web.config) but are located in different installation folders.

title: Load Balancing - Change the User Interface Configuration File
answer: To configure the User Interface Web.config file for load balancing: (1) Open the User Interface's Web.config file in editable mode. (2) Set the shared drive path with: <add key="AppContentPath" value="<shared drive path>" /> (the shared drive path was set up when configuring the shared network drive). (3) Comment out the sessionState timeout line: <!--<sessionState timeout="40" />-->. (4) Uncomment the Redis session-state section. (5) In that section, set the customProvider value to "RedisCacheAzure01". (6) Comment out the line beginning <add name="LocalRedisCacheAzure01" type="Microsoft.Web.Redis.Redis.........>. (7) In the <add name="RedisCacheAzure01" ...> line, set the Redis host, port, and access key (password) values.

title: Load Balancing - Change the Service Configuration File
answer: To configure the Service's Web.config file for load balancing: (1) Open the Service's Web.config file in editable mode. (2) Set the shared drive path for the workspace folder using the same path assigned earlier: <add key="WorkspaceFolder" value="%public%Documents">. (3) Set the EnableLoadBalancer key to true: <add key="EnableLoadBalancer" value="true">. (4) Set the Redis storage value's host, port, and password - these values were determined when installing the Redis Server earlier in the load-balancing setup.

title: How to Change the Color (RGB) Value for a Work Item
answer: To change the color displayed for a work item: (1) Go to <Installation Drive>:\Program Files\Modern Requirements\Modern Requirements4DevOps 2019\User Interface\App_Data. (2) Open ColorCodeMapping.xml in Notepad. (3) Change the desired color code for the work item. (4) Save the file (if you lack admin rights, save it to the desktop first and then replace the existing file in the same folder). (5) Restart IIS for the change to take effect.

title: How to Update the Work Item Type for Simulation, Diagram and Usecase
keywords: work item to file type mapping
simulation diagram usecase work item type
answer: Modern Requirements4DevOps has a default mapping embedded to support the "Work Item to File Type" functionality; when a new file is created, a page work item is generated in the connected team project using the work item type defined in this mapping. To change the mapped work item type: (1) Go to <Windows installation folder>\Program Files\Modern Requirements\Modern Requirements4DevOps 2019\Service\App_Data. (2) Open the XML file "WIToFileTypeMapping". (3) In the relevant module's section, find the field <WorkItem id="<WI Type>" /> and update the "<WI Type>" value. (4) Save the file to another location (e.g., desktop). (5) Copy the saved file back into the original installation folder, replacing the existing file. (6) Restart the application service from IIS Manager. (7) Log in to the application. To restart the service: open "inetmgr" to launch IIS Manager, select the "Modern Requirements4DevOps 2019 Service" option on the left, then under "Manage Web Site" on the right, click Stop followed by Start.

title: How to Change the Location of the Baseline File (Workspace Folder)
answer: Modern Requirements4DevOps creates a local working folder on the install machine; changing its location is recommended primarily at first installation, since manually relocating it afterward makes all existing project data and files inaccessible (existing content cannot simply be copied to the new location, and altering or removing files at the current location can corrupt project data). To change the location: (1) Go to <Installation Drive>:\Program Files\Modern Requirements\Modern Requirements4DevOps 2019\Service. (2) Open web.config and find the tag <add key="WorkspaceFolder" value="%public%/Documents"/>. (3) Update the "WorkspaceFolder" value to the required location (this can be a shared data drive or a separate drive/folder). (4) Save web.config. (5) Restart the IIS service. Warning: doing this on an existing installation will make all previously created project data and files inaccessible.

title: How to Delete Obsolete NFR Templates from the FAQ Module
answer: Obsolete NFR templates can appear when creating a new topic in the FAQ Module. These leftover templates come from a folder created during installation of older versions of the product (previously named inteGREAT4TFS). To remove them, manually delete this folder: C:\Users\Public\Documents\inteGREAT4TFS\QWizard Templates\NFR. After deleting the folder, re-sign in or refresh the application to confirm the obsolete templates are gone.

title: Deployment Instruction Page Appears Instead of License Status Page (Embedded)
keywords: visual studio team services license status
answer: In the Embedded version, you can check license status by browsing to <machine name>:8028/License/Status (e.g., steve:8028/License/Status), which normally shows the license status page. Sometimes the deployment instruction page appears instead. This happens when you are using Visual Studio Team Services but have not yet used any Modern Requirements4DevOps module in the current session - i.e., you are in the container environment but have not actually opened Modern Requirements4DevOps, so the license status check does not work yet. Once you click into any Modern Requirements4DevOps module, this issue no longer occurs.

title: Troubleshooting the "Unexpected Error" Message (Standalone)
answer: If you see an "unexpected error" message on the Sign-in page (Standalone version), resolve it as follows: (1) On the Sign-in page, click the "Click here" link. (2) You will be taken to the Diagnostics page, which describes the precise root cause of the error. (3) Click the "click here for solution" link to be redirected to the solutions page, where detailed solutions for the identified root cause are listed. (4) Follow the provided solution to resolve the problem.

title: Troubleshooting "IIS Version is Lower.." Error
answer: If installation fails with the message "ModernRequirements4DevOps cannot be installed on system with IIS Services version lower than 7.0," possible causes are: (1) IIS is not installed on the target machine, (2) IIS was not properly or completely installed, or (3) IIS is installed but the version is below 7.0. The recommended fix is to install IIS Manager completely, ensuring the installed IIS version is greater than 7.0.

title: Troubleshooting "400 Bad Request" Error (Embedded)
answer: Internet Explorer by default blocks cookies from sites loaded inside an IFrame when that site's domain differs from the parent site's domain. In the Embedded version, the parent site is https://*.visualstudio.com while the IFrame site is https://modernrequirements.info, causing a "400 Bad Request" error - this issue is specific to Internet Explorer (Firefox and Chrome are unaffected). The fix requires configuring IIS to send a custom P3P response header, on every IIS server where the Embedded version is deployed: (1) Open IIS Manager and select the server name at the Root. (2) Double-click "HTTP Response Headers". (3) Click "Add" in the Actions panel. (4) Enter Name = p3p and Value = CAO PSA OUR, then click OK. (5) Select the server name in Root again. (6) Restart IIS.

title: Enabling HTTPS and Changing the Port for Modern Requirements4DevOps
answer: By default the Modern Requirements4DevOps service runs on port 8028 (accessed as <Host Name>:8028). To enable HTTPS and/or use a custom port: (1) Open IIS Manager via "inetmgr". (2) Expand the root node, then expand the Sites node. (3) Right-click the "Modern Requirements4DevOps 2019" site and select "Edit Bindings". (4) In the Site Bindings dialog, click Add. (5) Change the binding type from http to https. (6) Provide the desired port number. (7) Select the SSL certificate to use. (8) Click OK. Afterward, Modern Requirements4DevOps is accessed via https://<host name>:<port number>.

title: Chrome Configuration for HTTPS Users
answer: Users accessing Modern Requirements4DevOps over HTTPS in Chrome need additional Web.config changes for the application to run correctly: (1) Open the Web.config file in the Modern Requirements installation folder. (2) Search for the tag containing "MRIsSecureSite". (3) Change the value of the "MRIsSecureSite" key to "true". (4) Search for the comment "<!-- For secure(https) site -->". (5) Uncomment the tag immediately below that comment. (6) Comment out the next line (which was previously active). (7) Save and close the Web.config file.

title: What is Modern Requirements4TFS Embedded
answer: Previously, Modern Requirements4TFS had a standalone user interface separate from Team Foundation Server (TFS) Web Access. As of Modern Requirements4TFS update 2, Modern Requirements4TFS supports a fully embedded, immersive experience directly within TFS Web Access, instead of requiring a separate standalone application window.

title: Which TFS version is needed to use the embedded version
answer: If your TFS version is older than TFS 2015 Update 2, you must use the standalone version of Modern Requirements4TFS — the embedded version is not available. If you have at least TFS 2015 Update 2, the embedded version becomes available and will show additional sub-hubs under the TFS Work hub.

title: Sub-hub capabilities added under the TFS Work hub (embedded, TFS 2015 U2+)
answer: For organizations on at least TFS 2015 Update 2, the embedded version adds sub-hubs under the TFS Work hub. This hub supports management of diagrams, mockups, use cases, reviews, and baselines. It also supports traceability analysis and reporting, and the generation of user-defined documents.

title: FAQ feature for requirements elicitation (2000+ questions, 14 NFR categories)
answer: The embedded hub uses an FAQ feature for requirements elicitation, working by answering questions collected by experts. There are over 2,000 questions catalogued across 14 NFR (non-functional requirement) categories.

title: TFS 2017 Update 1: create a diagram against work items and preview in Backlog
answer: If you have TFS 2017 Update 1, the embedded version provides further integration points. One of these is the ability to create a diagram directly against a work item and preview that diagram directly in the Backlog view.

title: TFS 2017 Update 1: Smart Report, Review, Baseline, and Impact Assessment from the context menu
answer: With TFS 2017 Update 1, the embedded version lets you generate Smart Reports, initiate Reviews, create a Baseline, and perform an Impact Assessment, all using the right-click context menu in both the Backlog view and the Query view.

title: TFS 2017 Update 1: Smart Report, Review, and Baseline from the query toolbar
answer: With TFS 2017 Update 1, the embedded version also lets you generate a Smart Report, initiate a Review, and create a Baseline directly from the query toolbar.

title: TFS 2017 Update 1: Invoke Impact Analysis from the work item form
answer: With TFS 2017 Update 1, the embedded version allows Impact Analysis to be invoked directly from within an open work item form.

title: Embedded feature availability: TFS 2015 Update 1 and older
answer: For TFS 2015 Update 1 and older, the embedded version is not available. You must use the standalone version of Modern Requirements4TFS.

title: Embedded feature availability: TFS 2015 Update 2 and newer
answer: On TFS 2015 Update 2 and newer (prior to TFS 2017), the embedded version has these feature limits: Toolbar Options in Queries are not supported; the Model (diagram) is not supported in Backlog; the Context Menu from Backlogs shows all options; and the Context Menu from Queries shows only Impact Analyzer.

title: Embedded feature availability: TFS 2017
keywords: context menu queries impact analyzer only
answer: On TFS 2017, the embedded version supports: Context Menu from Queries shows only Impact Analyzer; Context Menu from Backlogs shows all options; Toolbar Options in Queries is supported; and Model (diagram) is supported in Backlog.

title: Embedded feature availability: TFS 2017 Update 1 (full support)
answer: On TFS 2017 Update 1, the embedded version has full feature support: Context Menu from Queries shows all options; Context Menu from Backlogs shows all options; Toolbar Options in Queries is supported; and Model (diagram) is supported in Backlog.

title: Embedded version availability for Visual Studio Team Services (VSTS)
answer: For Visual Studio Team Services (VSTS), use the standalone version of Modern Requirements4TFS. If you prefer an embedded version for VSTS, you should contact Modern Requirements directly.

title: Word Import Configuration Overview and Supported Word Versions
answer: This document defines standard rules of Work Item Mapping Configuration supported in the Modern Requirements application, to help users define mapping in a ruleset file. By providing mapping configuration in a ruleset file, a user can import Microsoft Word document content into Smart Docs in the form of ADO work items. A ruleset file can be created either manually (as XML) or from the UI using the Ruleset Designer. Supported Microsoft Word versions for Word Import are Microsoft Word 2010 or higher, with the .docx, .dotx, .docm, and .dotm file extensions. The document is organized into: Key Points (for Ruleset Designer UI and for XML file/manual), Ruleset Designer UI, Work Item Mapping Configuration (supported by both XML manual and Ruleset Designer UI) for Headings, Tables, List Paragraph, and Add Paragraph, and an Appendix.

title: Key Points for Ruleset Designer (UI) - Supported Word Content
answer: Before importing, users should review the Word document to determine what content should be managed as Work Items or fields in Smart Docs after import. Users can import a Word document using ruleset files created through the Ruleset Designer, accessible from the Word Import wizard window: Import Ruleset tab > Ruleset file (dropdown). The following Word document content is supported from the UI: Heading style (H1-H9), Table (row, cell), List Paragraph (Add List), and Add Paragraph.

title: Key Points for XML Ruleset File (Manual) - Setup and File Locations
answer: For the manual XML approach, users should first review the Word document to know what content should be managed as Work Items/fields. Users can import using default configuration ruleset files, accessible from Word Import wizard window > Import Ruleset tab > Ruleset file (dropdown). To define custom mapping, create a ruleset file with the '.wirule' extension and place it at one of these locations depending on deployment: dev.azure.com version - %public%\Documents\inteGREAT4TFS\My Ruleset\Smart Docs\dev.azure.com\{Account}; visualstudio.com version - %public%\Documents\inteGREAT4TFS\My Ruleset\Smart Docs\{Account}.visualstudio.com; Embed version - %public%\Documents\inteGREAT4TFS\My Ruleset\Smart Docs\{Server Name} or ...\{Server Name}\{Collection Name}. After placing the custom ruleset file at one of these locations, it becomes accessible from Word Import wizard window > Import Ruleset tab > Ruleset file (dropdown) > Smart Docs (node).

title: XML Ruleset File - Required Tags (witype, property, propertytype) and Supported Content
answer: Content supported in the XML (manual) ruleset file: Heading style (H1-H9), Paragraph, Table (row, cell), and List Paragraph. To provide mapping, users must use the 'Field name' of the work item/field as defined in the TFS process template. For mapping, the following general tags/attributes are required: 'witype' (if mapping to a work item type) and 'property' (if mapping to a field of a work item) - 'property' can also be used as a tag to define more than one property of a work item. It is necessary to specify the 'value' of the field, which can only be set to either 'string' or 'html' type. If 'propertytype' is not defined for a field, the system considers it a 'String' type field by default.

title: Ruleset Designer User Interface Overview
answer: The document refers users to an embedded PowerPoint file, 'Word Import Configuration - Ruleset Designer.pptx', for more details regarding the user interface accessibility of the Ruleset Designer.

title: Headings: Map Each Heading Style to a Different Work Item Type
answer: To map each heading style to a different work item type, the heading name should map to the 'Title' field, and the content/paragraph written under the heading should map to any HTML field of the work item. Each heading node (Heading1, Heading2, and so on) must be selected individually to map it to a different work item type.

title: Headings: Map All Headings to the Same Work Item Type Using the 'Headings' Tag
answer: To map every heading style to the same work item type (for example 'Requirement') rather than mapping each heading individually, use the 'Headings' tag to map the same work item type at all headings defined in the document. Once the 'Headings' tag is defined, individual headings (H1-H9) can no longer be defined separately; instead, the sub-add dropdown will only show 'Add Table' and 'Add List' as available options.

title: Headings: Map the Same Heading Into Multiple Work Item Types Using a Condition (Usecontent)
keywords: same heading different work item types
answer: To map the same heading style into two or more different work item types, a condition must be defined (using content, i.e. 'Usecontent') to differentiate between occurrences of the same heading. This is configured consistently across the sample Word document, the manual ruleset XML file, and the ruleset file generated from the Ruleset Designer. A note in the document clarifies that this same configuration approach also applies when using the 'Ends with' condition.

title: Headings: Map a Table Placed Under a Heading Into the Work Item's HTML Field
answer: To map a table placed underneath a heading into that heading's work item HTML field, the ruleset (via Ruleset Designer or manual XML) is configured so the table content nested under the heading is captured into the HTML field of the same work item created for that heading.

title: Tables: Map an Entire Table to a Single Work Item Using Merged Cells
answer: To map an entire table to a single work item whose fields are formed from merged cells, the table is configured so that the whole table becomes one work item with its (merged) cell content mapped to the work item's individual fields.

title: Tables: Map Each Row to a Work Item and Each Column to a Field (Ignoring the Header Row)
answer: To map each row of a table to the same work item type, with each column mapped to an individual field of that work item, configure row/column mapping accordingly (do not map the header row itself to a work item). To exclude the header row of a table from being mapped to any work item type, check the 'Ignore this row' checkbox under 'Row Rules' in the right panel of the Ruleset Designer.

title: Tables: Map a Whole Column with Different Values Using Usecontent
answer: To map a whole table column where different values in that column should be handled/mapped differently, define 'Usecontent' for the column so that its content determines the resulting mapping. This is shown in the sample document, the Ruleset Designer configuration, and the manual XML file.

title: Tables: When the Usecontent Checkbox Is Enabled and Its Section Hidden
answer: The 'Usecontent' checkbox is only enabled (with its section hidden) when a table is defined at the top node level or as a child of a heading; it is also enabled with the section hidden at the row level.

title: Tables: Map Each Row of a Table to a Different Work Item Type
keywords: row to different work item type
answer: To map each row of a table to a different work item type (rather than mapping all rows to the same type), the configuration is shown via the sample Word document, the Ruleset Designer example, and the manual XML ruleset file.

title: List Paragraph: Map Each List Item Individually to a Different Work Item Type
answer: To map each list paragraph (bullet or numbered item) to a different work item type, each list paragraph node must be selected individually so it can be mapped to its own distinct work item type.

title: List Paragraph: Map All List Items to the Same Work Item Type via 'Apply to all lists'
answer: To map every list paragraph (all bullets/numbering) in the document to the same work item type (for example 'Epic'), check the 'Apply to all lists' checkbox in the right panel of the Ruleset Designer.

title: List Paragraph: Map a Hierarchy of List Items to the Same Work Item Type via 'recursive'
answer: To map list paragraphs defined in a hierarchy (nested lists) to the same work item type (for example 'Epic'), check the 'recursive' checkbox in the right panel of the Ruleset Designer so the same work item type is applied throughout the hierarchy defined in the document.

title: List Paragraph: Map Bullets/Numbering Within the Same List to Different Work Item Types via Usecontent
answer: To map bullets/numbering within the same list paragraph to different work item types, define 'Usecontent' at the list level and also check the 'Apply to all lists' checkbox in the right panel, so that all bullets/numbering defined in the document are mapped according to the content-based rule.

title: List Paragraph: Map a Single List Item Into Multiple Fields via 'Import list as'
answer: To map a single list paragraph into multiple fields (for example, part of the paragraph's content into one field and the remaining content into another field), check the 'Import list as' checkbox in the right panel of the Ruleset Designer.

title: Add Paragraph: Map Each Paragraph to a Different Work Item Type with Multiple Fields
answer: To map each paragraph to a different work item type where the paragraph's content is split across multiple fields (for example, part of the content into one field and the rest into another), each paragraph node must be selected individually to map it to its own work item type. For each paragraph, the 'Import list as' checkbox in the right panel is checked by default (to support mapping a single paragraph into multiple fields), and the 'Title' field is selected by default in that dropdown.

title: Add Paragraph: Map Paragraph Content to Different Work Item Types Using Usecontent
answer: To map content within the same paragraph to different work item types, define 'Usecontent' at the list level and check the 'Apply to all lists' checkbox in the right panel, so that all bullets/numbering (paragraph content) defined in the document are mapped according to the content-based rule.

title: Appendix: Notification Message on Opening an Existing Ruleset File
answer: If a notification message appears when selecting and opening an existing ruleset file, it means the contents placed in that ruleset file are not yet supported by the Ruleset Designer UI (for example, because the file was created or edited manually with configuration the UI designer cannot represent).

title: What is Modern Requirements4DevOps NextGen (Getting Started overview)
answer: Modern Requirements4DevOps NextGen is a web-based requirements management tool that bridges traditional requirements management practices with agile DevOps methodology, streamlining collaboration, communication, and traceability between development and operations stakeholders. It manages various components within Azure DevOps Team Projects, and lets users: create Smart Documents, create and manage application mock-ups, create and manage baselines, create and manage traceability among work items, and request/manage reviews of work items from team members. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Getting_Started.htm

title: Document Management module overview (NextGen)
answer: The Document Management module lets users upload, organize, and manage documents and folders within a Team Project. Check-out/check-in functionality supports collaborative work with version control, and the system keeps a document version history so users can select and restore a previous version. MS-Word documents can be compared side-by-side across different versions. The interface also supports viewing, renaming, and removing documents and folders. To access it: go to the Boards section of your project and select 'Document Management'. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Document_Management.htm

title: Copilot4DevOps functions and where to access them (NextGen)
answer: Copilot4DevOps offers 16 distinct functions — including Elicit, Analyze, Impact Assessment, Q&A Assistant, Dynamic Prompt, and Convert — accessible via a pop-up menu. It can be opened from: the Queries or Backlog tabs (select a work item, open its '...' context menu, choose Copilot4DevOps), from Smart Docs files (via the toolbar or a grid work item's context menu), or via a dedicated Copilot4DevOps icon in the toolbar. In Version Packages, users open/create a package, then select a work item from the grid to add descriptions or data via Copilot4DevOps. The Convert function can transform content into user stories, use cases, and Gherkin format. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Copilot4DevOps.htm

title: Copilot4DevOps behavior on locked work items (NextGen)
answer: For locked work items, all the add/update options in each Copilot4DevOps function are shown disabled, with limited exceptions — such as creating a linked item, or using Convert to create a brand-new work item (rather than updating the locked one). See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Copilot4DevOps.htm

title: Smart Import: turning Word/PDF documents into work items (NextGen)
keywords: upload parse map classify link preview import
answer: Smart Import transforms a Microsoft Word (.docx) or PDF document into Azure DevOps work items, through a six-stage wizard: Upload, Parse, Map & classify, Link, Preview, and Import. Start by clicking 'New Import' on the Smart Import browse page. On the Upload page, add a document by dragging it into the upload area or using the browse button — accepted formats are .docx and .pdf, up to 50 MB each. After uploading, you can replace or delete the file. A saved ruleset template can be selected from 'Select Ruleset Template' to reuse a previous mapping configuration. Clicking 'Parse Document' (enabled only after a file is uploaded) extracts the document's structural outline and text content. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Smart_Import.htm

title: Version Packages module overview (NextGen)
answer: Version Packages is a module in Modern Requirements4DevOps NextGen that acts as a central place for creating and managing distinct version-package entities within a Team Project. Access it via Boards > Version packages, which opens a Browse Page for viewing and managing existing version packages. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Version_Packages.htm

title: Smart Docs module overview (NextGen)
answer: Smart Docs is the module for creating virtual documents that distribute information to all stakeholders, helping prevent misconceptions. It supports formal documentation aligned with CMMI methodology, and Agile/Scrum teams can use it to maintain supplementary documentation such as stand-up/daily-scrum notes. The Version Management feature lets users manage multiple versions of a document. Access it via Boards > Smart Docs. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Smart_Docs.htm

title: Review module overview and how it's invoked from Baseline/Smart Docs (NextGen)
answer: The Review module manages reviews of work items within a Team Project — users can request reviews from teammates and complete reviews assigned to them. Access it via Boards > Review, or create a review request directly within the module. Review can also be invoked from other modules: from Baseline, invoking Review automatically adds the relevant work items into the Create Request dialog's corresponding section; from Smart Docs, invoking Review skips showing the 'Add Work Item' section entirely because the relevant work items are added automatically in the background, fully pre-populated. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Review_Management.htm

title: Trace Analysis module overview (NextGen)
answer: Trace Analysis manages traceability between work items. It supports generating an Intersection Traceability Matrix and a Horizontal Traceability Matrix. Within the matrix, users can edit work items directly, view each work item's current state, see existing links between work items, and create or delete links. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Traceability.htm

title: Baseline module overview (NextGen)
answer: The Baseline module is the primary tool for maintaining baselines of Team Projects: users can create new baselines, compare baselines to identify differences, generate Difference Reports documenting those variations, and compare work item revisions. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Baseline.htm

title: Diagrams module overview (NextGen)
answer: The Diagrams module lets users create, modify, and publish diagrams — including connected diagrams and sub-diagrams — within Azure DevOps. It's accessed by clicking the Diagrams tile on the NextGen main page, and serves as a design space for conceptual system models (as opposed to Mockups, which are physical/visual representations). Business Analysts use Diagrams to brainstorm and develop system models for stakeholder review, feedback, and discussing system improvements. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Diagram.htm

title: Reporting module overview vs. reports from other modules (NextGen)
answer: The Reporting section is dedicated to creating Advanced Reports, which are designed by the user from scratch rather than from predefined templates, giving full control over report content and presentation. Reports can also be initiated from other modules within the application, not just from Reporting itself. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Reporting.htm

title: Generating a Smart Report: window, report parts, and style sheets (NextGen)
answer: Smart Report is accessible across all modules for personalizing report formatting before generation. Open a document and click the 'Smart Report' option in the toolbar to open the Smart Report window. Select a Report Part from a dropdown with IntelliSense search, choose a Style Sheet, then click 'Generate Report'. Reports default to HTML format but can also be saved as MS Word or PDF. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Generating_Smart_Report.htm

title: Exporting and saving a Smart Report: Word templates, PDF, and Save to Library (NextGen)
keywords: export smart report word pdf html
save as pdf as word template
answer: A generated Smart Report can be exported as MS Word, PDF, or HTML. For Word output, a custom template can be uploaded to personalize headers, footers, and the table of contents (uploaded templates can also be deleted from the template management interface). To get a PDF that preserves a Word template's formatting, use the 'Save as' menu and choose 'PDF as word template'. The 'Save to Library' option stores the generated report directly in the Document Management module, via a dialog where you set the report title, destination folder, and format. Large datasets trigger background processing (the app stays usable while the report generates), and an email with a link to the report is sent once a bulk report completes — the size threshold that triggers this is configurable in the system configuration file. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Generating_Smart_Report.htm

title: Smart Edit / Smart View: side-by-side work item comparison and where it's available (NextGen)
keywords: side by side comparison work item
smart edit review baseline smart docs version packages
extension point context menu smart edit
answer: Smart Edit (Smart View) enables side-by-side comparison of different versions/variants of a work item. It's integrated into several modules: the Review module (for version comparison during review), Baseline (for baseline-related comparisons), Smart Docs, and Version Packages (for package version analysis). It's also reachable via the extension point in the work item context menu, both in Backlogs and in Queries. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Smart_View.htm

title: Linked Artifacts: read-only lookup of where a work item is used (NextGen)
keywords: where is this work item used
baseline review smart docs version package sections
work item form menu linked artifacts
answer: Linked Artifacts is a read-only lookup — it does not create, change, or remove any link — that shows where a selected work item is used across modules: Baselines, Reviews, Smart Docs, and Version Packages. It's opened by right-clicking a work item in Queries or Backlog (or from a work item form menu) in Azure DevOps, and from context menus on work item rows in Smart Docs, Baseline detail grids, and Version Package Result tabs. The dialog header shows the work item's type, ID, and title. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Linked_Artifact.htm

title: Linked Artifacts dialog: sections, opening results, and limitations (NextGen)
answer: The Linked Artifacts dialog organizes results into four collapsible sections — Baseline, Review, Smart Docs, and Version Package — toggled open/closed by clicking each group header. Selecting an artifact opens it in a new browser tab within its own module (artifacts from other projects also open in a separate tab). A Refresh button re-runs the lookup; Maximize/Restore buttons resize the dialog for large lists; a Close button dismisses it. In Version Package Result tabs specifically, Linked Artifacts only works on locked packages and saved versions — not on root rows or multi-row selections. All labels are available in 14 supported languages. See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Linked_Artifact.htm

title: Admin Panel: six configuration sections, including the newer Copilot4DevOps tab (NextGen)
answer: In NextGen, the Admin Panel is accessed by launching the embedded application and selecting 'Modern Requirements4DevOps' under the Settings tab. It has six sections: Licensing (check license status, activate with a valid key), General (app-wide settings, including repository name configuration for GIT projects), Smart Docs (module-specific settings), Baseline (module-specific settings), Review (module-specific settings), and Copilot4DevOps (configure and manage integration with Copilot4DevOps Plus — this tab is new compared to older Admin Configuration Guide versions of the Admin Panel). See: https://www.modernrequirements.com/help/modern-requirements4devops-nextgen/Admin_Panel.htm
